Since inception, in Kallakurichi Constituency of Tamil Nadu, 62 roads of 257 km length and 3 bridges have been constructed with an expenditure of Rs.184 crore under various verticals of the PMGSY. The State/UT-wise, District-wise and Parliamentary Constituency-wise details of rural road projects and the stages of construction under various verticals of PMGSY may be accessed at the programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb on a real-time basis.

Under PMGSY-I, out of total 1,63,275 sanctioned habitations, 162,845 habitations (99.7%) have been provided connectivity. The road works for providing connectivity to balance 401 habitations are at various stages of execution.

In September 2024, the Government of India launched PMGSY IV. The primary objective of PMGSY IV is to provide all-weather road connectivity to about 25,000 unconnected habitations of population size (as per Census 2011) 500+ in plains, 250+ in Special Category States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Ladakh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu Kashmir and Uttarakhand), Special Category Areas [(Tribal Schedule-V Areas, Desert Areas, Aspirational Blocks/ Districts and Hilly areas as notified by the respective State Government (cross slope more than 25% gradient and the elevation is more than 600 meters from the Mean Sea Level)] and 100+ in LWE affected Districts including Legacy & Thrust Districts identified by MHA from time to time. Under PMGSY-IV, habitations identified under VVP-II are being prioritised for all-weather road connectivity. Under PMGSY IV, the States/UTs have surveyed 41,200 habitations for connectivity which are further scrutinized by National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA) and sanctions are given based on the Detailed Project Reports sent by the State/UTs. Till date, 6752 road works of 19,643 km and 94 bridges have been sanctioned which will provide connectivity to 7455 habitations.

As per PMGSY guidelines, ensuring the quality of road works and maintenance of roads constructed is the responsibility of the State/UT Governments. However, the Department of Rural Development conducts quality assessment through National Quality Monitors (NQMs) and monitors maintenance of roads and bridges through compulsory routine inspections on the eMARG digital platform.

All PMGSY works are covered by initial five year maintenance contracts during the Defect Liability Period (DLP) as per the Standard Bidding Document. Maintenance funds to service the contract are required to be budgeted by the State/UT Governments and placed at the disposal of the State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDAs) in a separate account. The routine inspections on roads are conducted on a bi-monthly basis and the expenditure is based on the performance. On expiry of the 5 years, during the post Defect Liability Period (post DLP), the roads are placed under Zonal maintenance contracts for a further term of 5 years, which includes renewal and maintenance from time to time. The budget for the same is also allocated by the State/UT governments.

The details of funds allocated, released and utilised under PMGSY during the last five years is given at Annexure.

Ministry of Rural Development has taken a number of initiatives to expedite completion of road works sanctioned under PMGSY:

(i) PMGSY has a robust mechanism in place to ensure effective monitoring and quality construction of works. To effectively monitor the scheme and bring about greater efficiency, accountability and transparency in implementation, a modern web-based Online Management, Monitoring, and Accounting System (OMMAS) has been set up for PMGSY. Implementation of all sanctioned works is being monitored through OMMAS on a real-time basis to ensure that the physical and financial progress are in sync with the overall targets given to states. Further, a Project Management Information System (PMIS) has been developed for better management of the construction activities of each road sanctioned under PMGSY-III.

(ii) To enhance transparency during road construction, it has been made mandatory to install Global Positioning System (GPS) enabled Vehicle Tracking System (VTS) on all vehicles/machinery/equipment deployed by the contractor/PIUs for execution of PMGSY works. This helps in assessing the proper operation of this machinery/equipment for a specified period, which is essential for achieving the specified quality of the roads being constructed.

(iii) Further, as a measure of further enhancing the focus on maintenance of roads during the defect liability period and also streamlining the delivery of routine maintenance of PMGSY roads, eMARG has been introduced, which is conceptualized on Performance Based Maintenance Contracts (PBMC). As mentioned in reply to (b) above, payment to the contractor is now made through eMARG, which is based on the condition of road, its cross drainage works and traffic assets. Payments are based on how well the contractor manages to comply with the performance standards or service levels defined in the contract.

(iv) Electronic Maintenance of PMGSY roads (e-MARG), an online platform, has been implemented in all the states/UTs to monitor maintenance of PMGSY works for five years from the date of completion (i.e. under Defect Liability Period- DLP). Consequent upon the introduction of e-MARG i.e. software module for maintenance payments to the contractor during the defect liability period, such payments have been made commensurate with the quality of roads through a performance-based contract management system.

(v) Programme is regularly monitored by way of Regional Review Meetings (RRMs), Performance Review Committee (PRC) meetings, monthly review meetings and Pre-Empowered/Empowered Committee meetings with the States/UTs. The State/UT Governments are also regularly advised to convene meetings with the concerned authorities to expedite matters relating to land issues, forest and wildlife clearances in order to expedite completion of works.

(vi) A recent initiative about provision of unique digital identity (QR code) to every PMGSY road marks a transformative shift in how rural infrastructure is managed. Under the framework, each road will be assigned a geo-spatial identification number linked to a QR code. This identity will be displayed on roadside signboards and backed by a digital record containing its location, classification and assset details. In effect, every road becomes a traceable, searchable entity in a national inventory. On scanning the QR code, the public can place the grievance through Meri Sadak mobile application as well as the CPGRAMS portal. All the complaints are redressed through digital systems in an accountable manner.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
LAUNCHING OF VB-G RAM-G SCHEME
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 in rural areas of the entire country. All States and Union Territories have notified Viksit Bharat G RAM G Scheme in accordance with the provisions of the Act, and have started implementing the same.

Certain expressions of views/concerns by some organisations in relation to the implementation of the VB–G RAM G Act have been reported in sections of the media. The concerns, inter alia, relate to the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, the continued demand-driven nature of the programme and the apprehension that a phase-wise implementation strategy may adversely affect employment opportunities for rural workers.

In this regard, it is stated that the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 preserves the statutory, demand-driven nature of the rural employment guarantee by providing 125 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The Act further strengthens the programme by placing greater emphasis on sustainable livelihood creation, durable and productive rural assets, water security, climate resilience, transparency and technology-enabled governance, while retaining the statutory right to demand employment and receive unemployment allowance in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

Under VB G RAM G, from July 1st 2026, over 99.5% workers who demanded employment have been offered employment and 5.20 Crore persondays have been generated across 8.46 lakh worksites as on 22.07.2026.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PESTICIDE MANAGEMENT BILL
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Pesticides Management Bill, 2026 has been drafted by Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare in alignment with current requirements as well as Jan Vishwas Act.

The draft Pesticides Management Bill was circulated to all Ministries/Departments and State/UT Governments on 30.12.2025 for comments and subsequently placed in the public domain on 07.01.2026, inviting comments from the general public and stakeholders including pesticide manufacturers and dealers/retailers. A large number of suggestions/ observations have been received from states/UTs and Ministries/Department, pesticide manufacturer associations, pesticide dealers, individual pesticide manufacturers, farmers, NGOs etc. on various aspects of pesticide management and regulation including data protection. 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
AGRICULTURAL INPUT SUBSIDY FOR HORTICULTURE CROPS
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

The cost of cultivation of horticultural crops such as orange, kinnow and cash crops like cumin and isabgol, is input and labour intensive due to requirement of quality planting material, fertilizers, irrigation systems and post-harvest infrastructure. On the requests received from various stakeholders and considering the increase in prices of various inputs and materials in the horticulture sector, operational guidelines of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) scheme were revised in 2025. Under the revised guidelines, the cost norms of various horticultural crops were enhanced, along with the introduction of the latest technologies used in the horticulture sector. A comparative statement on enhanced support is as per Annexure.

As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for natural calamities of ‘severe nature’ and is approved on the basis of a Memorandum received from the State Government, in accordance with established procedures. The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief and not as compensation. The detailed items and norms are available on the Disaster Management Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs website: ndmindia.mha.gov.in.

 

Annexure

Comparative table of Old vs New Guidelines under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) support for Orange, Kinnow, Cumin and Isabgol cultivation:

Crop/

Category under MIDH

Old Guidelines (2014)

New / Revised Guidelines (2025)

Fruit Crop (Citrus)

including Orange and Kinnow

 

Under high density, the Cost norms is ₹1.00 lakh/ha without integration and ₹1.50 lakh/ha with drip integration for orchard establishment. The subsidy given is @40% (general areas) and @50% (NE/hilly areas). Max area: 4 ha/beneficiary.

Higher cost norms for orchard establishment (without drip) and for Regular spacing - ₹1.25 lakh/ha) Support for high-density - ₹2.00 lakh/ha and for Ultra-high density - ₹3.00 lakh/ha with same subsidy pattern (40–50%).

Seed Spice including

Cumin

 

Cost norm: ₹30,000/ha with subsidy @40% in general areas and @50% in NE/hilly areas. Max area: 4 ha/beneficiary.

Cost norms was revised upward to ₹50,000/ha for improved seed, INM, IPM, and scientific cultivation practices.

Medicinal & Aromatic Plants

including

Isabgol

 

Medicinal plants were not included in the earlier guidelines.

Cost norm is ₹1.50 lakh/ha with subsidy @ 40–50% depending on region for support of quality planting material, cultivation, and value-chain development.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
STRENGTHENING OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETING
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

Agricultural Marketing is a State subject. Government of India has been supporting states to strengthen agricultural marketing and ensure fair and remunerative prices to farmers through policy measures and schemes.

Government of India initiated National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), an all-India electronic trading (e-trading) portal by virtually integrating Physical Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs). The platform provides farmers access to a larger pool of buyers through transparent online bidding, better price discovery and direct payment of sale proceeds into their bank accounts. The platform also facilitates inter-State trade by enabling buyers across the country to participate in online bidding. As on 30th June, 2026, 1.89 crore farmers and 2.78 lakh traders are registered on e-NAM. Inter-State trade on e-NAM has increased from 563 MT (₹37 lakh) in 2018-19 to 2,984.3 MT (₹14.28 crore) in 2025-26, with cumulative inter-State trade of 28,566 MT valued at ₹83.95 crore. The average number of trader bids per lot has increased from 2.1 in 2016-17 to 2.8 in 2025-26, indicating increased competition among buyers.

Under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), 10,000 FPOs have been registered across the country. The FPOs collectivise farmers for aggregation of produce to leverage economies of scale and increase bargaining power of member farmers. Since launch of the scheme in 2020, the total cumulative turnover of FPOs has crossed Rs.20,340 crore.

To strengthen post-harvest management, logistics, storage and value addition, under Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) Scheme, 12,353 storage infrastructure projects with storage capacity of 369.18 lakh MT and 6,901 non-storage projects have been sanctioned in last ten years. Under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) interest subvention support has been extended to 18,893 warehouses, 3,110 cold stores/cold chain projects and 2,105 integrated primary and secondary processing units. Under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) component, about 1.76 lakh infrastructure units, including pack houses, cold storages, refrigerated vans, ripening chambers, pre-cooling and processing units have been created.

Ministry of Food Processing Industries has been implementing Central Sector Umbrella Scheme-Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) to create, interalia, post-harvest infrastructure and processing facilities to boost the overall development of the food processing sector. As on 30th June, 2026, 1256 projects have been completed or are operational, benefitting about 37.76 lakh farmers. 

World's Largest Grain Storage Programme is implemented by Ministry of Cooperation for storage infrastructure at PACS level, enabling farmers to store produce, avoid distress sales, improve access to remunerative markets and reduce dependence on intermediaries. Construction work has been completed in 313 PACS creating a storage capacity of 1.80 LMT.  

NITI Aayog in its evaluation report of 2020 and 2025 has recognized the Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) as a relevant intervention for strengthening agricultural marketing through improved market infrastructure, competitive markets and better price realization for farmers. The Scheme has promoted market reforms, FPO-led aggregation, value addition and development of post-harvest infrastructure. The reports further observe that grading units and storage facilities performed better where integrated with horticulture clusters and linked with active FPOs and SHGs, improving utilization and visibility. It also noted that more than 60 per cent of beneficiaries reported using post-harvest infrastructure and crop processing facilities under ISAM. Beneficiaries recognized improvements in price realization, product longevity and market appeal through value addition. The evaluation highlighted the potential of e-NAM in promoting transparent markets, efficient price discovery, better contract negotiations and improved access to institutional finance. Overall, ISAM has contributed to strengthening agricultural marketing infrastructure and improving market efficiency. 

Agriculture is a State subject. Government of India supplements efforts of the States through a comprehensive range of Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes and programs aimed at increasing production, productivity, farmers’ income etc. across the country. These schemes encompass entire spectrum of agriculture, including credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops (including horticulture), seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, extension, digital agriculture and procurement of crops.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Such support is provided through State Horticulture Missions, Technical Support Groups (TSGs), Precision Farming Development…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Support to Farmers under MIDH
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

Government is implementing the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for holistic development of the horticulture sector in the country. Under MIDH, institutional, technical and extension support is provided to assist farmers in the adoption of protected cultivation technologies. Such support is provided through State Horticulture Missions, Technical Support Groups (TSGs), Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of Excellence (CoEs), ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other recognised institutions.

The National Horticulture Board (NHB) also provides institutional and technical support through implementation of programmes such as the Clean Plant Programme, Horticulture Cluster Development Programme. Centres of Excellence established under MIDH serve as demonstration and training centres and act as sources of elite planting material and vegetable seedlings under protected cultivation. Sixty-one (61) crop-specific Centres of Excellence have been established under MIDH through Indo-Israel Cooperation, Indo-Dutch Cooperation and Research Institutes. In addition, assistance is available for demonstrations, capacity building and training of farmers and field functionaries under the Human Resource Development (HRD) component of MIDH.

The Operational Guidelines of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) do not contain any specific provision for engagement of NGOs or private sector entities. However, under Mission Management component of MIDH, 2.5% of total annual allocation is provided to State Horticulture Missions for managing various activities at State & District level.

MIDH scheme also provides support for strengthening institutional support framework for protected cultivation through Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of Excellence (CoEs), State Horticulture Missions, National Horticulture Board (NHB), ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities and Krishi Vigyan Kendras. Further, financial and technical assistance is provided under MIDH for construction of protected cultivation structures like poly house, shade net house, plastic/non-woven cloth tunnels, walk in tunnels etc.

Apart from the above, assistance is provided for promotion of protected cultivation at commercial scale through National Horticulture Board (NHB) for establishment of integrated commercial horticulture production/processing projects including components such as planting materials, plantation, irrigation, fertigation, mechanization etc.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
DISCREPANCY IN FERTILIZER QUALITY TESTING
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

As per existing provision of Fertilizer Control Order (FCO), 1985 which was amended on 13-12-2024, out of the three samples collected by the Fertiliser Inspectors, one sample is given to the dealer or importer or manufacturer or pool handling agency or marketer as the case may be and the second sample is sent to the in-charge of the laboratory and the third sample is kept in the custody of designated authority appointed by the State Government.

In case the sample is reported as non-standard then within a period of fifteen days from the receipt of the report, the dealer or manufacturer or importer or pool handing agency or marketer, as the case may be, will have to apply to the designated authority appointed by the State Government for re-testing along with the prescribed fee and the sample provided to him by the Fertiliser Inspector. The designated authority of the State Government shall immediately send any of the two samples that is one submitted by the dealer or manufacturer or pool handling agency or importer or marketer and other lying in its custody to the National Test House (NTH), Ghaziabad Coding centre for testing at any of its Centre at Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Jaipur and Ghaziabad for second analysis.

The report of National Test House shall be treated as final and in case there is variance in first and second analysis report that is the sample reported as non-standard in different parameters, then the designated authority of state Government shall suo motto send the sample lying in their possession for third analysis at Central Fertiliser Quality Control and Training Institute, (CFQCTI), Faridabad and the analysis report of the Institute shall be treated as final:

However, if  the dealer or manufacturer or pool handing agency, as the case may be, does not apply within the stipulated period of fifteen days then the report of first analysis shall be final. In case where the sample reports that is first analysis report and second analysis report are declared as non-standard in a common parameter, in such case, there shall not any third analysis and the report of the second analysis shall be treated as final.

The detail of samples received and test results for 2nd analysis  by NTH and 3rd analysis by CFQC&TI are as under-

Under clause 30 of FCO, 1985, the time limit is prescribed for analysis and communication of results. As per this clause, for 2nd testing, the designated officer of State Government shall send the sample for analysis at NTH, within a period of three working days from the date when the concerned manufacturer, dealer, importer, pool handling agency or marketer applied for referee analysis. NTH shall analyse the sample within a period of fifteen days from the date of receipt of sample in the laboratory and also communicate the results. In case samples failed in different parameters, the designated officer of State Government within three working days shall send the sample to Central Fertiliser Quality Control and Training Institute, Faridabad for third analysis. The laboratory shall analyse the sample within a period of fifteen days from date of receipt and communicate the results to concern designated authority of State Government, within a period of three working days from the generation of report. The designated officer of State Government shall communicate the result to the concerned party within the period of three working days from the date of receipt of report.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.title: PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE AND SEEDS
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE AND SEEDS Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi The Government has taken several measures for conservation, research, production, value addition and promotion of traditional agricultural produce and indigenous/local crop varieties in the country. These measures include: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), through the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR) and its network of research institutes, undertakes exploration, collection, exchange,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE AND SEEDS
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken several measures for conservation, research, production, value addition and promotion of traditional agricultural produce and indigenous/local crop varieties in the country. These measures include:

  1. Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), through the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR) and its network of research institutes, undertakes exploration, collection, exchange, characterization, evaluation, conservation and documentation of indigenous germplasm.
  2. Intellectual Property Rights are granted to traditional and farmers’ varieties under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001. As on 15th July, 2026, 5346 farmer’s varieties have been registered by PPV&FR Authority belonging to traditionally cultivated varieties and landraces.

National Gene Fund has been established under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, with the aim of promoting conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources, including traditional varieties. It seeks to reward and incentivize farmers and communities engaged in conservation, improvement, and preservation of plant genetic resources through benefit-sharing, awards, and recognition schemes, while also supporting capacity building activities to safeguard agro-biodiversity. So far, 45 Plant Genome Saviour Community Awards, 69 Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Reward and 88 Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Recognition have been conferred to farmer(s)/ farming communities across the country.

  1. A component namely "Boosting Seed Production of Traditional Varieties" under the Seeds component of the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) has been introduced, aimed at promoting traditional varieties of crops. Under this intervention, financial assistance is extended for seed distribution, seed production, capacity building, and the creation/development of seed banks for traditional varieties, in accordance with prescribed cost norms.
  2. To promote the 'Vocal for Local' initiative in the food processing sector, the PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach, aimed at fostering balanced regional development across all districts of the country for supporting district-specific agricultural and horticultural products, including traditional and indigenous produce. ODOPs have been approved for 726 districts across 35 States/UTs, including traditional and indigenous products e.g. Makhana, Shahi Litchi, Jardalu Mango. The PMFME Scheme provides financial, technical and business support for processing, value addition, packaging, branding and marketing of these products including traditional produce.
  3. Traditional agricultural products possessing unique geographical characteristics are also protected through registration under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, administered by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), thereby strengthening their identity, branding and market value.
  4. In addition, traditional agricultural products are promoted through commodity-specific Boards and agencies such as the Tea Board, Coffee Board, Spices Board, APEDA and the National Medicinal Plants Board under their respective schemes for quality improvement, branding, value addition, export promotion and market development. Recently, Government has established National Makhana Board for production, processing, value addition, and marketing of makhana.
  5. Special thrust has been given to traditional millets ("Shree Anna") through the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission, following the observance of the International Year of Millets. Indian Institute of Millets Research (ICAR-IIMR) in Hyderabad, India, serves as the designated Global Centre of Excellence on Millets for promotion of international research and development in millets.
  6. Under Production Linked Incentive scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), following the UN’s declaration of 2023 as the “International Year of Millets”, a dedicated Millet-Base Products (PLISMBP) component was added to incentivize value addition and commercialization of millets.

Government incentivizes and supports research aimed at improving indigenous/local varieties of agricultural produce and seeds. The details and steps taken are as under:

  1. ICAR-IARI is implementing 13 dedicated research projects, supported by ICAR, DBT and DST, for characterization, evaluation and utilization of indigenous germplasm, landraces and wild relatives in crops such as wheat, rice, maize, sesame, lentil, cucumber and tomato. The projects focus on agrobiodiversity, germplasm evaluation, molecular breeding, genomics and genome editing for developing improved, climate-resilient and disease-resistant crop varieties.
  2. At ICAR-IARI, research on improving the traditional Basmati varieties has led to the development of improved Pusa Basmati rice varieties which accounts for dominant share of India’s Basmati exports.
  3. Two high yielding varieties, namely Pusa Narendra KN1 and Pusa CRD KN2 have been released targeting specific Geographical Indication areas in eastern Uttar Pradesh, promising improved yield and non-lodging trait against the traditional landrace “Kalanamak”.
  4. ICAR-NBPGR documents genetic resources, maintains inventories and brings them into the public domain, facilitating their safe and accelerated use in research and crop improvement. This enables researchers and breeders to access indigenous germplasm for varietal improvement. As on 15th July, over 1 lakh landraces/traditional varieties are conserved in the National Gene Bank.
  5. Under the joint work plan between Alliance Bioversity-CIAT and National Agricultural Research System under the aegis of ICAR, promotional activities such as documentation of over 5,000 native varieties of 25 crops and evaluation across 11 states using participatory varietal evaluation (crowdsourcing) is undertaken, resulting in the identification of nearly 300 superior traditional varieties for large-scale cultivation. Further, nearly 50 Community Seed Banks have been established across India, conserving more than 4,000 traditional varieties of over 25 crops under this plan. In addition, nutritional profiling of more than 3,000 traditional varieties supporting branding and commercialization of indigenous produce and linking it to value chains, with brands such as Native Basket, Mountain Grains, Dhartee Naturals etc. have also been undertaken.
  6. Ministry of Food Processing Industries R&D scheme (component of the Human Resources & Institutions component of Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana) has approved 257 R&D proposals to date – several directed at traditional/indigenous produce (millet based products, mahua, drumstick etc.)

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY)
AB PM-JAY Achieves Pan-India Implementation; Now Operational Across All 36 States/UTs
AB PM-JAY Facilitates Nationwide Healthcare Access Through Portability; 29.05 Lakh Inter-State Admissions Worth ₹8,383.97 Crore Authorized
Health Assurance Extended to 6 Crore Senior Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above
Health Coverage Network Strengthened; Beneficiary Base Rises from 10.74 Crore to 12 Crore Families
Seamless Inter-State Portability Under AB PM-JAY Facilitated by Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras Through Beneficiary Verification, Cashless Admissions and Hospital Support
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) continues to strengthen India’s journey towards Universal Health Coverage by ensuring access to quality, affordable and cashless healthcare services. The scheme is now being implemented across all 36 States/Union Territories, marking a significant milestone in expanding healthcare access and strengthening the delivery of secondary and tertiary care services across the country.

Initially, the scheme covered 10.74 crore families identified under the Socio-Economic Caste Census, 2011, constituting the bottom 40% of India’s population. In January 2023, the beneficiary base was revised from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families to account for India's decadal population growth. In March 2024, approximately 37 lakh additional families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers were included under the scheme. The scheme was further expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status.

Further, many States have expanded the beneficiary base beyond the centrally targeted beneficiary numbers by converging their state-specific schemes with AB PM-JAY. The expansion of the beneficiary base under AB PM-JAY, coupled with the integration of various State health assurance schemes, has significantly enhanced the scheme's outreach among vulnerable populations across the country.

AB PM-JAY provides a national portability feature, enabling beneficiaries to avail cashless treatment at any empanelled hospital across the country, irrespective of their State/UT. This portability feature enhances access to quality healthcare services, particularly for migrant workers and beneficiaries travelling outside their home State.

As on 30th June, 2026, a total of 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 8,383.97 crore, have been authorized under AB PM-JAY across the country.

AB PM-JAY is implemented through a robust end-to-end digital platform that enables empanelled hospitals to identify and verify eligible beneficiaries, irrespective of their home State, and facilitates hospital admissions, claims processing and settlement for portability cases. This integrated digital ecosystem ensures seamless, cashless and paperless access to healthcare services at empanelled hospitals across the country.

To improve beneficiary enrolment and enhance awareness, including on the portability feature, AB PM-JAY has adopted a comprehensive Information, Education & Communication (IEC) and outreach strategy. The strategy includes awareness campaigns through traditional and digital media platforms such as newspapers, community radio, television and radio campaigns, digital displays, street plays, mass messaging, social media, and the dissemination of beneficiary testimonials.

Further, Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras deployed at empanelled hospitals play a key role in facilitating portability under AB PM-JAY. They assist beneficiaries, including migrant workers and those seeking treatment outside their home State, with identification and verification, cashless admission, hospital coordination, and support throughout the hospitalization process.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Prataprao Jadhav, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

*****

SR

HFW/Update on AB PM-JAY/28July2026/5

item.title: Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases
item.category: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals, 27 Apex Referral Laboratories and Real-time IHIP Monitoring Strengthen Disease Surveillance Nationwide Supply of Drugs, Diagnostics and Technical Guidelines Enhances Early Detection, Treatment and Outbreak Response Integrated Vector Management Through Indoor Residual Spraying, Bed Nets, Anti-larval Measures and Source Reduction Capacity Building, IEC/BCC Campaigns and Multi-sectoral Convergence Drive Community-based Prevention Across the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon-Related Diseases
887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals, 27 Apex Referral Laboratories and Real-time IHIP Monitoring Strengthen Disease Surveillance
Nationwide Supply of Drugs, Diagnostics and Technical Guidelines Enhances Early Detection, Treatment and Outbreak Response
Integrated Vector Management Through Indoor Residual Spraying, Bed Nets, Anti-larval Measures and Source Reduction
Capacity Building, IEC/BCC Campaigns and Multi-sectoral Convergence Drive Community-based Prevention Across the Country
Focused Interventions for Dengue, Malaria, Diarrhoea and Leptospirosis Supported by PPCL, STOP Diarrhoea Campaign and Flood Preparedness Measures
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has undertaken several measures to prevent and control the spread of monsoon-related diseases in the Country that include:

  • For early diagnosis and complete treatment of malaria, drugs and diagnostics are supplied to the States/UTs through the National Health Mission.
  • For surveillance and free diagnosis of Dengue, a network of 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals (SSHs) and 27 Apex Referral Laboratories (ARLs) identified across the country. GoI provides IgM test kits to all identified laboratories through the National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune.
  • A network of 5 diagnostic labs has been strengthened under the PPCL programme by providing Grant-in-Aid (GIA) for procurement of Equipment’s and consumables.
  • Capacity building and training of trainers, community leaders, and frontline workers to enhance outreach at the grassroots level.
  • Integrated Vector Management including Indoor Residual Spray in selected high-risk areas, Bed Nets in high malaria endemic areas, use of larvivorous fish, anti-larval measures in urban areas, including bio-larvicides and minor environmental engineering and source reduction for prevention of breeding.
  • STOP Diarrhoea Campaign” is conducted which aims at reducing illness and preventing deaths due to Diarrhoea among children under five years of age. The campaign follows the Protect, Prevent and Treat (PPT) strategy and promotes early management of Diarrhoea through Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) and Zinc supplementation.
  • Disease Management involving early case detection with active, passive and sentinel surveillance followed by complete and effective treatment, strengthening of referral services, epidemic preparedness and rapid response.
  • Supportive Interventions aiming at Information Education and Communication (IEC) & Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) and dissemination of public health messages through various media platforms including social media, radio, newspapers, and electronic media.
  • States are trained to enter the data on Integrated Health Information Portal-Vector Borne Diseases (IHIP-VBD) portal for real-time monitoring,
  • Provided Technical Guidelines for case management, prevention and control to the States for implementation.
  • Inter-Sectoral Convergence including high-level advocacy with allied Ministries, Human Resource Development through capacity building and policy development.
  • The Government is actively collaborating with State Health Departments and Urban Local Bodies to enhance sanitation, strengthen mosquito control measures, and increase public awareness for the prevention and control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases (VBDs).
  • Inter-departmental coordination, involving Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Public Distribution System (PDS) members, and religious/community leaders to mobilize communities and promote preventive practices.
  • Advisories are regularly issued to States and Union Territories including to continue promotive, preventive, and curative measures, including outbreak containment.
  • The advisory on leptospirosis emphasizes strengthening case-based surveillance through IDSP, timely reporting, and dissemination of clinical management guidelines with early antibiotic use and ensuring lab preparedness with diagnostic kits like IgM ELISA.
  • National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) is implementing Programme for Prevention and Control of Leptospirosis (PPCL) with aim to reduce morbidity and mortality by strengthening surveillance and diagnostic capacity, raising awareness on early detection and treatment, improving patient management facilities, capacity building and enhancing inter-sectoral coordination for effective outbreak prevention and control.
  • Management of urban flooding falls under the purview of the State Governments and the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India provides financial and technical support to the States for strengthening Urban Planning ecosystem. It supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions and issuing various documents/advisory guidelines for improving urban drainage and flood management.
  • Time-to-time advisories/guidance are issued to States/UTs by MoHFW, Government of India for actions to be taken for prevention and control of VBDs and other monsoon-prone diseases in flood-affected areas ensuring rapid deployment of response teams, maintain adequate stocks of diagnostic kits, drugs, insecticides and strengthen disease surveillance systems, close monitoring of situation for early detection and containment of outbreaks.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

 

****

SR

HFW/Measures Taken to Prevent and Control Spread of Monsoon Related Diseases /28July2026/3

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Steps taken to strengthen financial assistance for critical diseases
Cashless treatment available for 1,961 procedures under Health Benefit Package-2022
AB PM-JAY expanded to cover 12 crore families; senior citizens and frontline workers also included
One‑time aid up to Rs. 15 Lakh via Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi; Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant (HMDG) offers up to Rs. 1.25 Lakh for poor patients
Health Benefit Package-2022 enables cashless treatment across 27 specialties, including major non-communicable diseases
Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) applications processed online through National Health Authority portal; offline submission also available
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has implemented several measures to strengthen financial assistance for the treatment of critical diseases by expanding the coverage of health schemes and enhancing access to cashless treatment and financial support. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) was launched in September 2018 to provide health coverage of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. Initially, the scheme covered 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families identified on the basis of deprivation and occupational criteria under the Socio-Economic Caste Census, 2011, in rural and urban areas. In January 2023, the beneficiary base was revised from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families to account for India's decadal population growth. To further strengthen beneficiary identification and expand coverage, alternative beneficiary databases, including the National Food Security Act database and other State-specific beneficiary databases having similar socio-economic criteria were adopted under the scheme.

In March 2024, approximately 37 lakh additional families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers were included under the scheme. The scheme was further expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status.

Under the National Master of Health Benefit Package (HBP-2022), cashless treatment is available for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties, covering a wide range of secondary and tertiary care services, including treatment for major non-communicable diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, chronic kidney disease, diabetes-related complications, stroke, chronic respiratory diseases, neurological disorders, liver diseases etc.

Government of India provides one‑time financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh under the Umbrella Scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) for the treatment of poor patients suffering from life‑threatening diseases related to the heart, kidney, liver, and cancer, etc., in Government hospitals/institutes with super‑speciality facilities, subject to fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed under the scheme guidelines.

Further, under the Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant (HMDG), financial assistance up to Rs. 1.25 lakh is provided to poor patients suffering from life‑threatening diseases to cover part of the expenditure on hospitalization/treatment in Government hospitals, in cases where free medical facilities are not available, subject to fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed under the scheme guidelines. To apply for assistance under the RAN Scheme, the Nodal Officer of RAN at the concerned Government hospital/institute is to be contacted, who facilitates processing of the case online through the National Health Authority IT portal. However, in case the hospital is not onboarded for online processing of cases under RAN, or encounters technical issues while processing the case online, the patient’s duly filled application in the prescribed format (available with the guidelines of RAN) is required to be forwarded through the treating hospital to the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare for consideration. Further details regarding RAN/HMDG schemes can be accessed at: https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/→ Offerings → Programmes → Poor Patients Financial Support.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

 

****

SR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Steps taken for Licensing Compliance and Formalisation of Small Food Vendors
Over 74.33 Lakh Active Food Business Licences and Registrations Issued Under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
FSSAI Simplifies Licensing Framework Through Perpetual Validity, Free Registration for Street Vendors and Tatkal Licensing
Government Promotes Formalisation of Food Businesses Through Deemed Registration and Simplified Licensing Reforms
Over 2.23 Lakh Food Samples Analysed; More Than 40,000 Non-conforming Samples Detected in 2025–26
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has undertaken several measures to strengthen food safety, simplify regulatory compliance and promote the formalisation of food businesses. FSSAI is mandated to lay down science-based standards for articles of food and regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure the availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption.

The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility of the Central and State Governments. To facilitate and encourage informal, small and petty Food Business Operators (FBOs) to come under the formal food safety and licensing framework, FSSAI has implemented the following key measures:

  • Introducing the provision for deemed registration of street food vendors, hawkers, food trucks, carts and similar food businesses registered under the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 to address the dual compliance requirements for street food vendors, registered with municipal corporation and town vending committee.
  • Street food vendors and hawkers are completely exempt from the FSSAI registration fee. Applicable for both new registrations and renewals, eligible vendors can obtain a 5-year registration certificate completely free of charge.
  • To reduce the regulatory burden on FBOs and promote ease of doing business, FSSAI has introduced perpetual validity for licences and registrations. Earlier, licences and registrations were required to be renewed periodically, with validity ranging from one to five years. Under the revised framework, licences and registrations will remain valid indefinitely, thereby eliminating the need for periodic renewals while ensuring continued compliance with the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations made thereunder.
  • Tatkal issuance of License/Registration has been implemented w.e.f. 28th June 2024 under certain kind of low-risk food businesses such as Wholesalers, Distributors, Retailers, Transporters, Storage without atmospheric control, Importers, Food vending agencies, Direct sellers and Merchant–Exporters.

The State-wise details of active Licences and Registrations issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are annexed at Annexure-I. Details of enforcement action taken for all non-conforming foods products (including adulteration) across the country (State-wise) in the last 5 years is annexed at Annexure-II, III, IV, V and VI respectively.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Prataprao Jadhav, stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices
item.category: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
item.description: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices Government committed to safeguarding the future of students and ensuring integrity, transparency and credibility of public examinations Amendment Bill Aims to Reward Merit and Strengthen Credibility of Public Examinations: Dr. Jitendra Singh Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Dr. Jitendra Singh Says Public Examinations Amendment Bill Will Further Strengthen Legal Framework Against Examination Malpractices
Government committed to safeguarding the future of students and ensuring integrity, transparency and credibility of public examinations
Amendment Bill Aims to Reward Merit and Strengthen Credibility of Public Examinations: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 is a significant step towards further strengthening the legal framework to curb examination-related malpractices and protect the interests of students and youth across the country.

Initiating the discussion on the Bill in the Lok Sabha, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the legislation reaffirms the Government's commitment to safeguarding the future of students and reflects Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's resolve to ensure that no one is allowed to compromise with the aspirations of the country's youth. He described the legislation as a milestone in strengthening the integrity of India's public examination system.

The Minister said incidents of question paper leakages and examination-related malpractices have occurred across different States over the years, highlighting the need for a comprehensive national legal framework. He noted that the Government enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 as the country's first comprehensive legislation to deal with unfair means in public examinations and is now proposing further amendments based on the experience gained during its implementation to make the law more stringent and effective.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Act covers examinations conducted by major recruitment agencies, including the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS), as well as the National Testing Agency (NTA) for higher education admissions. He recalled that the 2024 Act made offences under its ambit cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable with stringent penal provisions.

Highlighting the key provisions of the Amendment Bill, the Minister said the punishment for persons resorting to unfair means is proposed to be enhanced from imprisonment of three to five years to five to ten years, while the maximum fine is proposed to be increased from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh. For service providers involved in such offences, the maximum fine is proposed to be increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore and the period of debarment from conducting public examinations from four years to eight years. Punishment for directors and senior management of service providers is also proposed to be enhanced from three to ten years' imprisonment to five to ten years, with the maximum fine being increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore. The Bill further proposes to increase the punishment for organised crime from five to ten years' imprisonment to seven to ten years and enhance the maximum fine from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore.

Emphasising the importance of speedy justice, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Amendment Bill provides for the establishment of Special Fast Track Courts to deal with offences relating to public examinations. He said the Bill envisages completion of investigation within two months and completion of trial within three months from the date of filing of the charge sheet, ensuring expeditious disposal of such cases. The Bill also empowers the Central Government to refer investigation of offences under the Act to a Special Task Force constituted for the purpose, thereby enabling swift and effective action against organised examination-related crimes.

The Minister informed the House that the Government has already initiated steps for establishment of Special Fast Track Courts in several locations to facilitate speedy disposal of such cases. He also referred to the Prime Minister's announcement of a high-level task force comprising eminent experts to make the public examination system "leak-proof". He added that substantial progress has already been made in implementing the recommendations of the committee constituted to strengthen the examination ecosystem. He said the objective of the amendments is to ensure that students are rewarded for their genuine efforts while enhancing the credibility, transparency and fairness of public examinations.

Concluding his remarks, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the proposed amendments would reinforce deterrence against organised examination-related crimes, ensure speedy justice and further strengthen public confidence in the integrity, transparency and fairness of the country's public examination system.

*****

NKR/AV

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Government Promotes Indigenous Potash Production and Alternative Nutrient Sources to Reduce Import Dependence
Potassium Derived from Molasses (PDM) Incentivised Under Nutrient Based Subsidy Scheme
GSI Intensifies Potash Exploration; ICAR Develops Potash Biofertilizers to Strengthen Self-Reliance
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has undertaken a series of initiatives to promote indigenous production of potash and develop sustainable alternatives to reduce the country's dependence on imported potash fertilizers. These efforts include incentivising the use of Potassium Derived from Molasses (PDM), intensifying domestic potash exploration, and promoting potash biofertilizers through scientific research and technological interventions.

Potassium Derived from Molasses (PDM) is a by-product of sugar industry. PDM has minimum 14.5% potash and can be used by farmers in field as an alternative to MOP (Muriate of Potash with 60% potash content). Thus, PDM reduces the dependence on imported potash. PDM was notified under Fertilizer Control Order (1985) in 2009, and in order to incentivize the use of PDM, it was inducted under Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme w.e.f. 13.10.2021.

In order to promote manufacturing and availability of PDM to the farmers as a sustainable, eco-friendly, and cost-effective alternative to conventional Muriate of Potash (MOP), a tune of Rs. 345 per tonne of subsidy has been fixed for PDM for Kharif, 2026 season. Further, to monitor the price of PDM, a Joint Working Group (JWG) of Department of Food & Public Distribution and Department of Fertilizers along with Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) & fertilizer companies has been constituted.

To enhance the domestic exploration of potash in the country in alignment with the objectives of National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM), Geological Survey of India (GSI) has intensified its exploration activities with special emphasis on the exploration of critical minerals in the country. Since the launch of NCMM in 2024-25, GSI undertook 8 exploration projects on potash in Rajasthan and Punjab. Further, during 2026-27, GSI took up 6 mineral exploration projects for potash in Rajasthan and Punjab. Since the Mines and Minerals Development and Regulation (MMDR) Amendment Act, 2015, GSI has established a total of 456.52 million tonnes resource of potash at various grades and different cut-offs from Rajasthan and Punjab.

To support self-reliance in potash production through indigenous and alternative nutrient sources, Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR) has identified and developed potassium-solubilizing microorganisms (Frateuria aurantia, Serratia liquefaciens and Bacillus sp), which are being promoted as potash biofertilizers to improve the availability of native soil potassium and reduce dependence on imported potash fertilizers.

This information was provided by Smt. Anupriya Patel, Minister of State in the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today.

***

Neeraj Kumar Bhatt/Shatrughna Prasad

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Government Ensures Adequate Fertilizer Availability Through Advance Planning, Real-Time Monitoring and Timely Imports
Integrated Monitoring and Coordinated Supply Mechanism Maintain Uninterrupted Fertilizer Availability Across States
Domestic Production and Strategic Imports Strengthen Fertilizer Supply During the Last Five Cropping Seasons
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has reiterated that a robust planning, monitoring and distribution mechanism is in place to ensure the timely and adequate availability of fertilizers across the country during every cropping season. Through advance assessment of demand, real-time monitoring of supplies, timely imports and close coordination with States and other stakeholders, adequate availability of fertilizers has been maintained across all States during the last five cropping seasons.

Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country:

  1. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the availability.
  2. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS).
  • III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizer is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance to ensure timely availability.
  1. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents.
  2. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States.
  3. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the concerned State government.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Promoting Agriculture Cooperatives in Hilly Areas
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Cooperation is providing assistance to promote cooperative agriculture, horticulture and marketing of allied products in hilly States, including Uttarakhand through National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory corporation under the Ministry of Cooperation. The State-wise details of financial assistance disbursed by NCDC during the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) to the hilly States/UTs, including Uttarakhand, are provided at Annexure-I.

Establishment of new offices of NCDC in hilly and remote areas, including Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, and Nagaland in addition to already existing offices in Assam, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand to improve service delivery and market support.

Ministry of Cooperation has established Bhartiya Beej Sahkari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), a multi-state cooperative society to provide quality, certified and affordable seeds to farmers. So far, BBSSL has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, and Uttarakhand for expanding the availability and marketing of quality seeds under the “Bharat Beej” brand across these states. 2,488 quintals of quality, certified and affordable seeds have been provided to the farmers in Uttarakhand thereby improving their access to quality seeds.

The steps taken by the Government to provide access to National and International markets to the products of hilly areas inter alia, include the following:

  • Establishment of National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) as an umbrella organization to export the goods and services of cooperative societies. So far, NCEL has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, and Uttarakhand to provide access to international markets to the products of the hilly areas.
  • Establishment of National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) as an umbrella organization for the procurement, aggregation, certification, testing, branding and marketing of organic produce. So far, NCOL has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, and Uttarakhand to provide market access to the organic products of the hilly areas. NCOL has procured around 417 Metric Ton organic wheat, 40 Metric Ton organic Basmati and 30 Metric Ton Sweeteners including Jaggery, Khandsari and Brown Sugar from organic certified farmers of Uttarakhand.

The member cooperative societies of BBSSL, NCEL, and NCOL benefit from access to quality, certified, and affordable seeds; assistance in quality testing and certification; access to national and international markets; better price realization for their produce; and dividends on their shareholding. The state-wise number of cooperative societies that have obtained membership in BBSSL, NCEL and NCOL is provided at Annexure-II.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Non-Registration of West Bengal Cooperatives
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi

The e-samyukti portal of National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India (NCCF) and e-samridhi portal of National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED) are open digital platforms on which all eligible PACS, Cooperative Societies, FPOs and farmers can register at any time. There are no state or region specific restrictions on registration. 62 PACSs and 10 PACSs from West Bengal have registered on e-samyukti and e-samridhi portals respectively.

Similarly, the membership in Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) and National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) is open to all cooperative societies across the country. 40, 12 and 4 cooperative societies from West Bengal are members of BBSSL, NCEL, and NCOL, respectively.

There is no denial of access to consumer retail networks, MSP procurement, organic certification, international export markets and affordable certified seeds respectively to the Cooperative Societies of West Bengal. NCCF has procured 257 Metric Ton of Maize from 148 farmers in West Bengal during Rabi Marketing Season 2025-26. NAFED has procured 1,800 Metric Ton of Maize from 237 farmers in West Bengal during Kharif-2024, Rabi-2025 & Kharif-2025 & Rabi-2026 seasons. 12 dealers of BBSSL are operating in West Bengal through whom 126 Metric Ton of seeds have been supplied to the farmers of West Bengal providing them access to quality, certified and affordable seeds.

The eligible PACS, Cooperative Societies, FPOs and farmers are continuously encouraged to register themselves on e-samyukti and e-samridhi portals through field level outreach activities and public awareness campaign.

In the Monthly state review meetings conducted by Ministry of Cooperation, all the states including West Bengal are requested to encourage the PACS to register on the said portals and obtain membership in BBSSL, NCEL and NCOL.

BBSSL, NCEL and NCOL have signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with West Bengal’s State Nodal Agency- West Bengal State Cooperative Marketing Federation Limited (BENFED) to closely coordinate with the state and reach out to the cooperative societies of the state.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Cooperative Sugar Mill
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

As per the information received from Government of Madhya Pradesh, there is no cooperative sugar mills in Tendukheda Assembly constituency of Narsinghpur district in Madhya Pradesh. At present, eight private sugar mills are operational in Narsinghpur district, out of which two sugar mills are functioning in the Tendukheda Assembly Constituency.

The Central Government does not set up Co-operative Sugar mill in any part of the country. As per the information received from Department of Food and Public Distribution, sugar industry was deleted from list of industries required compulsory licensing, vide press note dated 31.08.1998.

Ministry of Cooperation has taken up steps to revive co-operative sugar mills in the country. National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization under the administrative control of Ministry of Cooperation provides financial assistance for the revival and modernization of cooperative sugar mills either directly to the Cooperative Sugar Mills (CSMs) or through the State Government for passing on the same to CSMs, with due-diligence and subject to the viability of the project as per NCDC guidelines.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Number of PACS in Ujjain
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

In Madhya Pradesh, 680 new Primary Agricultural Credit Societies have been established/registered. 22 PACS have been established/registered in Ujjain District (since calendar year 2025).

In Ujjain District the total sanctioned PACS are 194 PACS in which total 172 are digitalized and computerized on a common Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) PACS Software.

As per information received from the State, as per Act and Bye-laws of M-PACS, all steps have been taken for the formation of M-PACS by Cooperative Department Ujjain. The Model Bye laws enable 25 plus activities for PACS including 22 M-PACS in Ujjain district.

Madhya Pradesh has reported surplus storage facilities in the state. So far, no location has been identified under the World's largest grain storage plan in Madhya Pradesh.

Under the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), financial assistance is released to States/Union Territories for implementation of the Project on a State-wise basis in accordance with the approved guidelines. The Project does not provide for separate earmarking or release of funds specifically for any particular district, including Ujjain. However, as per information received from the State, under PACS Computerisation project, hardware and software implementation for 172 PACS is done in Ujjain and GoI share (60%) of Rs 2.22 crores is used till date. National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) (as on 30.06.2026), has also disbursed financial assistance amounting to ₹0.52 crore during the last five years for the development of cooperatives in Ujjain district osf Madhya Pradesh.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Proposal for Insurance Company
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

In order to realize the vision of Sahakar-se-Samriddhi, Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the cooperative sector and deepen its reach up to the grassroot level across the country. These initiatives are aimed at promoting cooperation based economic development model, including socio-economic upliftment of small and marginal farmers, traders and other weaker sections.

The Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several initiatives to enable cooperative banks to carry out banking and allied financial activities at par with commercial banks, including acting as 'Corporate Agents' for the distribution of insurance products. These initiatives are aimed at diversifying the business portfolio of cooperative banks, strengthening their financial viability and competitiveness, enhancing fee-based income, and promoting financial inclusion. Further, these measures have ensured the expansion of access to and availability of quality banking and insurance services through the cooperative banking network, particularly in rural, semi-urban, and underserved areas.

Further, with the efforts of the Ministry of Cooperation, RBI has also removed the requirement of a minimum net worth of ₹50 crore for Rural Cooperative Banks to obtain a Corporate Agent licence for the distribution of insurance products, thereby facilitating greater participation of cooperative banks in insurance sector and expanding access to insurance services.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

Under the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, 1,015 PACS across the country have been identified for construction of godowns and construction work has been completed in 313 PACS creating a total capacity of 1.80 LMT. The State-wise details of the godowns constructed are enclosed at Annexure-I.

A total of 36 PACS have been identified by the State of Bihar. Out of these, a total of 27 PACS, including 4 from the West Champaran district, have applied for assistance under the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) scheme. Construction work has commenced at the 4 PACS in West Champaran district.

The Plan entails creation of various agri infrastructure including godowns, custom hiring centers, processing units, Fair Price Shops, etc. at PACS/ other cooperative societies level through convergence of various existing schemes of the Government of India (GoI), such as, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme (AMI), Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME), etc.  The modifications made in the guidelines is enclosed at Annexure-II.

This plan has been integrated with the storage requirement of the Food Corporation of India (FCI). FCI has mapped a storage requirement of approximately 26.03 LMT across 216 potential locations in 18 States/Union Territories. The Food Corporation of India has provided uniform hiring assurance for 9 years to the warehouses with a capacity of 2,500 metric tonnes or more (1,671 metric tonnes and above for North-Eastern and hilly regions)

  • To enhance the financial viability of the scheme, the margin money requirement has been reduced from 20% to 10%.
  • The construction cost has been revised from ₹3000–3500/MT to ₹7000/MT for plain areas and from ₹4000/MT to ₹8000/MT for northeastern states.
  • The subsidy has been increased from 25% to 33.33% (from ₹875/MT to ₹2333/MT for plain areas and from ₹1333.33/MT to ₹2666/MT for northeastern states).
  • For PACS, a provision has been made to provide an additional subsidy of 1/3 (one third) of the total admissible subsidy for ancillary infrastructure such as internal roads, weighbridges, boundary walls, etc.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Availability of Bharat Taxi in Purvanchal Areas of UP
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, registered under the MSCS Act 2002. Bharat Taxi is providing its services in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat and Maharashtra. At present, it has not been officially launched in Uttar Pradesh especially in Purvanchal.

The Government has not incurred any expenditure on the development, promotion, maintenance, or operation of Bharat Taxi. Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) funds the development promotion, maintenance and operation of Bharat Taxi through its own capital.

The performance of the Bharat Taxi Application is reviewed periodically by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL). The review covers key operational and service-related parameters, including customer experience, grievances received, fare competitiveness, platform performance, and the effectiveness of technology systems. The Application is also benchmarked against prevailing practices in the taxi aggregation sector to identify areas for improvement.

Based on the findings of such reviews and feedback received from users, appropriate corrective measures are undertaken, wherever required. These include strengthening the technology platform, addressing software-related issues, enhancing platform features, reviewing fare-related aspects, and improving service delivery. Regular technical and operational monitoring is also carried out to support the reliable and efficient functioning of the platform.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

*****

The State-wise details are enclosed as Annexure - I.

For the promotion of the 'Bharat Beej' brand of Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), 33 States/UTs have nominated nodal agencies including the States of Maharashtra and Rajasthan and 26 States/UTs have signed Memorandum of Understanding. The State-wise details are enclosed as Annexure - II.

So far, National Co-operative Exports Limited (NCEL) has exported 14,89,102 metric tonnes of 50 agri-commodities valued at ₹5,866.10 crore to 38 countries. During the Financial Years 2023-24 and 2024-25, NCEL passed on a dividend of ₹8,31,34,024 (20% on the paid-up value of the share capital held by its members) to its members.

NCOL and NCEL facilitate the aggregation and procurement of organic and other agricultural produce, respectively, while providing value-added services such as quality testing, branding, packaging, certification, and domestic and international marketing. BBSSL ensures the availability of quality, certified, and affordable seeds to farmers. Across the country, including tribal-dominated areas such as Palghar in Maharashtra and the State of Rajasthan, the majority of the members of NCEL, NCOL, and BBSSL are Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), whose membership predominantly comprises small and marginal farmers, thereby ensuring that the benefits of these initiatives reach small and marginal farmers.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
REVAMPED RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj has been implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/UTs. The number of participants trained, including elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries under the scheme of RGSA, State/UT-wise, including Himachal Pradesh, during the last three years is at Annexure-I.

The details of funds released to the State of Odisha and Himachal Pradesh, during the last three years are as under:

(Rs. in crore)

Himachal Pradesh
