item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
PMMSY IN KERALA
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Government of India through its schemes, policies and programs has been taking up several initiatives towards holistic development of fisheries sector in all the States and Union Territories (UTs) including in Kerala. During last 5 years and current financial year under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) fisheries developmental projects amounting to Rs.1413.91 crore has been approved to the Government of Kerala. Under the PMMSY, the district wise allocation and beneficiary selection are done by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. The Government of Kerala has informed that out of the total projects approved to Kerala under PMMSY, projects amounting to Rs. 8.85 crore has been allocated to the Ernakulam Parliamentary Constituency, and out of this Rs. 8.62 crore has already been released. The year-wise details of the funds allocated and released towards Ernakulam Parliamentary Constituency as reported by Government of Kerala is annexed.       

The Government of Kerala has also informed that the activities have been approved under PMMSY in Ernakulam inter-alia include Biofloc culture, Re-Circulatory Aquaculture System (RAS), brackishwater farming, cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish marketing kiosks and  Matsya Seva Kendras. It is also informed that the approved projects are in various stages of implementation.

(c) There is no proposal pertaining to Ernakulum constituency is pending in the Department of Fisheries, Government of India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
TRADITIONAL FISHERFOLK IN KERALA
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various schemes for holistic development of fisheries sector in all States/UTs including Kerala. The major schemes include Blue Revolution Scheme (2015-16 to 2019-20), extending Kisan Credit Card (KCC) to fisheries (since 2018-19), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) (2018-19 to 2025-26), ‘Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana’ (PMMSY)’ (2020-21 to 2026-27), and a new Central Sector Sub-scheme viz. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27). Enhancing fish production, ensuring sustainability of resources, strengthening of value chain, employment generation, safety & security of fishers and socio-economic wellbeing of fishers and fish farmers have been the core of these initiatives.

During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, DoF, GoI has accorded approvals to the fisheries development proposal of Government of Kerala amounting to Rs. 1413.91 crore. The approved activities inter-alia include livelihood support to fishers during fishing ban period, support to traditional fishers for procurement of boats and nets, establishment of integrated modern coastal fishing villages, establishment of climate resilient coastal fishing villages, additional and alternate livelihood activities such as bivalve cultivation, cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish markets & kiosks, cold chain facilities, live fish vending centres, need based training and skill development programmes and development of fishing harbours and marketing facilities etc.

 The Central Government allocates Superior Kerosene Oil (SKO) on a quarterly basis, but its distribution within a State/UT under the Public Distribution System (PDS) is entirely managed by the respective State/UT Government. The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) being the nodal Ministry on the subject matter has informed that as kerosene is a polluting fuel and adversely impacts public health, the PDS Kerosene allocation to States/UTs including Kerala have been rationalized since 2010-11. Till date, 21 States/UTs have become PDS Kerosene free. Government has formulated a new “PDS Kerosene Allocation Policy” for the period of 2025-26 to 2027-28 after stakeholders consultation including the Government of Kerala. As per the said Policy, the allocation is made to States/UTs under single category “PDS SKO” on quarterly basis for cooking & lighting and for special needs. Further, the State Governments have been given the liberty to sub-allocate PDS SKO for cooking and lighting or for special needs (fisheries, mela, exhibitions, pandemic, calamity etc.) based on their specific requirement. Distribution of PDS SKO within State/UT under PDS network is carried out by concerned State/UT. Scale and Criteria of distribution is, accordingly, also decided by respective State/UT.

MoPNG has further informed that under the new policy, the Government of Kerala has been allocated 22,704 KL PDS SKO for the year 2025-26 as against total allocation of 4,368 KL PDS SKO for the year 2024-25 which reflects an increase of 419.78 %. During the FY 2025-26 out of the allocated quantity of 22,704 KL the State uplifted 17,724 KL with a lapse of 4,980 KL.

It is also informed that, in view of the prevailing geo-political situation an adhoc allocation of 1716 KL PDS SKO was also made for cooking and lighting to the State vide MoPNG’s letter dated 12.03.2026 for upliftment till 30th June 2026. Out of the allocated quantity, the state uplifted 1512 KL only lapsing 204 KL. Further, an allocation of 4068 KL/quarter has been made to the State of Kerala for Q1 (April-June, 2026) and Q2 (July-September, 2026), 2026-27.

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
BLUE ECONOMY PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) has been implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):  A scheme to bring about Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible development of fisheries sector in India’ in all States and Union Territories (UTs) including the State of Andhra Pradesh, since 2020-21. Under PMMSY, for the development of fisheries and fisheries infrastructure in the State, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has approved proposals of the Government of Andhra Pradesh at a total cost of Rs 2328.89 crore, with a central share of Rs 681.38 crore. An amount of Rs 445.05 Crore has been released to the State based on the State's utilization. The year-wise details of projects approved, fund sanctioned and released during the last six years under PMMSY for furnished at Annexure I.

 The major fisheries infrastructure projects approved under PMMSY for development of fisheries in the State of Andhra Pradesh include (i) establishment of 5 fish feed plants, (ii) 16 cold storages and ice plants, (iii) 6 modern fish landing centres, (iv) 3 modern fishing harbours, (v) modernization of fishing harbour at Vishakhapatnam and (vi) 1 integrated Aqua Park. In addition, 15 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) and one Fish Brood Bank have also been sanctioned.

 The Government is closely monitoring developments in the global trade environment, including geopolitical situations, through regular engagement with stakeholders and export promotion agencies. While no separate State-specific assessment has been carried out on the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood exports from Andhra Pradesh, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has undertaken several initiatives to address emerging trade challenges. These initiatives include a Seafood Exporters Meet in April 2026, New Delhi and National Workshop on Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh in June 2026, wherein issues relating to market diversification, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), non-tariff barriers, traceability, logistics and export competitiveness were deliberated with stakeholders. Despite the prevailing global geopolitical and trade challenges, various efforts taken by the Government of India has resulted in India's seafood exports recording an all-time high of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes valued at ₹73,890.46 crore (US$ 8.46 billion) during the financial year 2025–26.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Flash Report on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects worth ₹150 crore and above
PAIMANA Portal tracks 1,847 Infrastructure Projects worth ₹40.54 lakh crore as of June 2026
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) continues to strengthen monitoring of Central Sector infrastructure projects through its PAIMANA platform, enabling improved tracking, timely reviews, and data-driven decision-making across Ministries. The portal tracks 1,847 Infrastructure Projects worth of ₹40.54 lakh crore as of June 2026.

Key Highlights

  • As of June 2026, 1,847 ongoing infrastructure projects, with a total revised cost of ₹40.54 lakh crore, are being monitored across 17 Central Ministries/Departments. The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stands at ₹21.97 lakh crore, accounting for approximately 54.18 per cent of the revised project cost, indicating steady progress in project implementation.
  • A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 709 projects (~39%) achieving over 80% physical progress, while 337 (~19%) have crossed 80% financial completion. The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation.
  • The Transport & Logistics sector (as per the DEA’s Harmonized Master List) accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1341 projects), with revised estimates of ₹22.32 lakh crore underscoring priority to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth.
  • 1,847 ongoing infrastructure projects include 769 Mega projects (project cost of ₹1,000 crore & above) with an original cost of ₹30.51 lakh crore, and 1,078 Major projects (project cost below ₹1,000 crore and up to ₹150 crore) amounting to ₹5.10 lakh crore.
  • Physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0–20%) and advanced (81–100%) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly-started projects alongside many nearing completions. While physical progress exceeds financial progress in the 81–100% range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation.

 

Ministry/ Departments-wise progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, with 1022 projects (55%), and a share of total revised project cost of ₹9.89 lakh crore (24%), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development.
  • Ministry of Railways is implementing 255 projects (14%), with a total revised project cost of ₹8.69 lakh crore (21%).
  • Ministry of Coal accounts for implementing 121 projects (7%), with a total revised project cost of ₹2.22 lakh crore (6%).
  • The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 105, 98, 50, and 40 projects, with associated revised costs of ₹4.33 lakh crore, ₹5.71 lakh crore, ₹3.65 lakh crore, and ₹2.04 lakh crore, respectively.
  • The remaining 156 projects (8%), with a total revised cost of ₹4.02 lakh crore (10%), are distributed across various Ministries/Departments including Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports. (Refer Annexure I)

Sector-wise (as per DEA’s Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure) Progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Transport & Logistics remains the dominant sector, accounting for 55% of total revised project cost (₹22.32 lakh crore) across 1,341 projects (73% of the total Projects), underscoring the central role of Roads & Highways, Railways, Aviation, Urban Public Transport, Shipping, and Inland Waterways in economic integration and logistics efficiency.
  • The Energy sector follows with 26% of aggregated revised cost (₹10.38 lakh crore) across 207 projects, reflecting sustained emphasis on Oil & Gas infrastructure, electricity generation, transmission and distribution networks, and energy storage systems.
  • Communication infrastructure, with a project cost of ₹2.64 lakh crore (7%) across 15 projects, represents targeted interventions aimed at strengthening digital connectivity.
  • Water & Sanitation projects account for ₹2.08 lakh crore (5%) across 56 projects, highlighting continued focus on essential urban services.
  • Social & Commercial infrastructure, comprising 88 projects with a revised project cost of ₹0.94 lakh crore (2%), reflects selective investments in education, healthcare, real estate, and tourism, hospitality and wellness.
  • Projects classified under ‘Others’, amounting to ₹2.18 lakh crore (5%) across 140 projects, indicate diversification across sectors such as coal, steel, metals, and mining.

(Refer Annexure II)

 

Completed Projects and New Additions

  • During June 2026, notable commissioned projects include-
    • Project – “Rajasthan Refinery Project” (₹ 79,459 crore) of Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas.
    • Project – “Transmission System for Kurnool Wind Energy Zone/ Solar Energy Zone Part-A and Part-B” (₹ 3,546.94 crore) of Ministry of Power.
    • Project - “6L of Varadharajula to Kumarajapet from km 0.000 to km 43.800 of NH-716B Pkg-I” (₹ 1,887.38 crore) and “Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway Phase-I Pkg-IV from Junction with Jind-Karnalroad NH-709A near Alewa village to Junction with Ambala-Kaithal-Hissar road NH-152 near Kharak Pandwa village Km 91400 to Km 120250” (₹ 1,578.66 crore) of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.
  • During June 2026, 17 additional projects were brought under the monitoring of PAIMANA. Of these 14 are from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway and 3 are from Department of Telecommunications. These include:
  • “6 Lane Greenfield Varanasi- Ranchi- Kolkata Highway from Donoreshan village to junction with  NH-20 in Bongabar village from km 288.600 to km 325.500 Pkg -11” (₹ 1,856.12 crore)
  • “6L Greenfield Varanasi- Ranchi- Kolkata Highway from junction with  NH-20 in Bongabar village to junction with NH-30 in Lepo village from km 325.500 to km 358.500 Pkg -12” (₹ 1,525.52 crore)
  •  “Development of 6-lane Greenfield Southern Ludhiana Bypass from intersection with NH-44 near Village Rajgarh to intersection with Delhi Katra Expressway NE-5 near Village Ballowal, km 0000 to km 25240” (₹ 1,424.55 crore).

Next date of Press Release: Flash Report for the month of July 2026 would be released on 25th August 2026.

Note

  1. PAIMANA is a centralized web-based portal for monitoring of Central Sector Infrastructure Projects costing ₹150 crore & above.
  2. The press release summarizes highlights from the MoSPI’s Flash Report (June 2026) on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects (₹150 crore and above), available at https://paimana-proj.mospi.gov.in/ or via the QR code.

 

  1. Nearly 70% of data are updated via API’s on PAIMANA-CRIP portal  that serves as a national central repository of infrastructure  projects contributing towards standardized infrastructure monitoring and support informed decision-making for nation-building.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
India's Index of industrial production records growth of 7.3% in June 2026
Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the Month of June 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

In June 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 7.3% year-on-year growth, supported by 7.8% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 10.6% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.

The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28th of every month (or next working day if 28th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.

2.  Key Highlights:

  1. The IIP growth rate for the month of June 2026 is 7.3 percent which was 5.1 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of May 2026.
  2.  The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 are 1.0 percent, 7.8 percent, 10.6 percent and 6.1 percent respectively.
  3. The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.1 against 114.7 in June 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 stand at 110.0, 123.3, 131.0 and 145.7 respectively.
  4. Within the Manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in June 2026 over June 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of June 2026 are – “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (34.0%), “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (17.5%), and “Manufacture of food products” (10.8%).
  5. In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment” item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives”, and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  6. In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers”, item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  7. In the industry group “Manufacture of food products”, item groups “Tea”, “Rice (Other Than Basmati)”, and “Starch, All Types” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  8. As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 119.5 for Primary Goods, 140.5 for Capital Goods, 124.2 for Intermediate Goods and 132.9 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month of June 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 119.8 and 115.4 respectively.
  9. The corresponding growth rates of IIP as per Use-Based Classification in June 2026 over June 2025 are 4.9 percent in Primary Goods, 14.2 percent in Capital Goods, 9.3 percent in Intermediate Goods, 7.5 percent in Infrastructure/ Construction Goods, 7.7 percent in Consumer durables and 4.9 percent in Consumer non-durables (Statement III).  Based on Use-Based Classification, top three positive contributors to the growth of IIP for the month of June 2026 are Intermediate Goods, Primary goods, and Capital Goods.
  1. Along with the Quick Estimate of IIP for the month of June 2026, the indices for May 2026 have undergone final revision in the light of the updated data received from the source agencies.
  2. The Quick Estimates for June 2026 and the final revision for May 2026 have been compiled at weighted response rates of 86.7 percent and 93.1 percent respectively.
  3. Details of Quick Estimates of the Index of Industrial Production for the month of June 2026 at Sector, Sub-Sector, 2-digit level of National Industrial Classification (NIC-2025), by Use-Based Classification and are given at Statements I, II (A, B, C, D) and III respectively. Also, for users to appreciate the changes in the industrial sector, Statement IV provides month-wise indices for the last 13 months, by industry groups (as per 2-digit level of NIC-2025), sectors and Sub-Sectors.
  4. Release of the IIP for July 2026 will be on Friday, 28th August 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
DEVELOPMENT OF RESERVOIRS AND AMRIT SAROVARS
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi

 (a): The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country including Bastar  constituency in Chhattisgarh. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihoods of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self-help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for the development of fisheries in Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. The key components of this initiative  includes strengthening quality seed production by establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value addition units.

(b) to (d): The selection of the Reservoirs and Amrit sarovars  by the  Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) has been done in consultation with States and Union Territories (UTs), considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. Accordingly, 12 number of reservoirs and 5 numbers of Amrit Sarovars from Bihar and 27 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars from Chhattisgarh including Kosardeda reservoir from Bastar Constituency has been selected. District-wise reservoir selected in Chhattisgarh in consultation with the State Government is at Annexure-III. 

(e) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fishers’ income in the country is promoting involvement of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars.

(f) The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars is to be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The  unit cost and funding pattern are as per the existing guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
GAIS FOR FISHERMEN
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total investment of Rs. 20,750/- crore from the financial year 2020-21 to till date for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories.  The scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre  and State in the ratio of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre. The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/- for permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs. 25,000/.  The year wise and State/UT wise details of claims filed, claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending, and total compensation disbursed under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for fishermen since 2020 21 are furnished at Annexure-I.

(b)       During the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) and current finance year (2026-27) of the implementation of the PMMSY, an average of 35.74 lakh active fishers have been enrolled under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS), annually. The average State/UT-wise details of fishers enrolled and coverage percentage of the total estimated fishermen population under Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) are furnished at Annexure-II.

(c):       Besides, under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme, insurance coverage for fishers was modest, with relatively lower benefit amounts. Based on the suggestions received from State Governments and evaluation of Blue Revolution Scheme, the GAIS coverage under PMMSY has been significantly enhanced both in scale and value to provide increased financial security and risk mitigation to fishers. As such, the sum assured has been increased from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability, ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability, along with ₹10,000/- to Rs. 25,000 hospitalization support, compared to much lower limits under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TAMIL NADU UNDER PMMSY
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

 (a): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) accorded administrative approvals for the implementation of projects under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in Tamil Nadu during the period 2020-21 to 2025-26 with a total approved outlay of Rs.1,240.5778 crore. This comprised a Central share of Rs.480.0906 crore, State share of Rs.455.6139 crore, and beneficiary contribution of Rs.272.8488 crore covering both Beneficiary and Non-Beneficiary components. The approved project outlay represents the total financial allocation for the entire scheme period, whereas the Central share is released in phases by the DoF, GoI based on the progress of implementation, submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs), and compliance with scheme guidelines, etc. Accordingly, the Central assistance is released from time to time, and it does not represent a deficit in the approved project outlay.

(b): The details of central funds released under PMMSY to Tamil Nadu, year wise during the last three years (2023-24 to 2025-26) and the details of central funds released under PMMSY in Tirunelveli District of Tamil Nadu are provided at Annexure. The subsidy amounts are directly transferred to the beneficiaries bank accounts through Electronic Clearing Service (ECS).

(c): To promote Deep Sea fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the DoF, GoI had introduced a sub-component namely “Assistance for Deep Sea Fishing” and another component of “Conversion of Trawlers into Resource Specific Deep-Sea Fishing Vessels” under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) on Blue Revolution implemented from 2015-2020. These sub-components were introduced to provide financial assistance to traditional fishermen for promotion of deep-sea fishing in the coastal States/UTs including Tamil Nadu. The financial assistance to traditional fishermen for acquisition of Deep Sea Fishing Vessels (DSFVs) has also been continued under the PMMSY at the rate of 40% subsidy for General Category and 60% subsidy for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries. Support for DSFVs is also provided by the DoF, GoI, under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF). Under PMMSY, financial support is provided to traditional fishers for acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels (DSFVs) as well as for Upgradation of Existing Fishing Vessels for Export Competency. Under the schemes of Blue Revolution, PMMSY, and the FIDF, projects amounting to Rs.1,314.81 crore have been sanctioned for the acquisition of 1,205 deep-sea fishing vessels by traditional fishers including the fishers of the Tamil Nadu State. The development and modernisation of infrastructure has been accorded high priority under the schemes implemented by the DoF, GoI. Infrastructure projects worth Rs 187.9 crores were sanctioned under Blue Revolution Scheme in Tamil Nadu, which includes fishing harbour project at Mookaiyur and fish landing centre at Kunthukal. Projects worth Rs 155.57 crores have been sanctioned under the PMMSY in Tamil Nadu, which includes three fishing harbour projects viz. modernization of Chennai fishing harbour, upgradation of Pazhayar fishing harbour, maintenance dredging of Colachel fishing harbour; and four fish landing centre projects viz. Nettukupam fish landing centre, Thazankuppam fish landing centre, Arangankuppam fish landing centre, and Goonankuppam fish landing centre. Under Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) scheme, 16 Nos of Fishing Harbours and 57 Fish landing centre have been sanctioned in Tamil Nadu at total project cost of Rs.1988.35 crore.

(d): The subsidy/concession rate on fuel to the fishermen has been provided by the respective State Governments/Union Territories, by exercising their powers to frame their own taxation and welfare policies for the fisheries sector. It is informed by the State Government of Tamil Nadu that the Government is providing sales tax exempted diesel to the fishermen for reducing the operational cost of their fishing boats (Both mechanized fishing boats and motorized country crafts) and also providing subsidized industrial kerosene to the motorized country crafts operated in the districts of Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts.

Under these scheme, Government of Tamil Nadu is providing sales tax exempted diesel of  19,000 L / year / craft to 4,500 Mechanised fishing boats, sales tax exempted diesel of  4,400 L / year / craft to 13,500 Motorized country crafts and subsidized industrial kerosene of 3,700 L / year / craft to around 7500 Motorized country crafts. 

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Makes Rooftop Solar Accessible for All with Subsidy Support and Low-Interest Financing
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

In order to ensure the affordability of rooftop solar (RTS) systems for middle-income and economically weaker households under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY), following provisions have been made:

  1. Higher central financial assistance for the first two kWp of RTS capacity.
  2. Availability of collateral-free loan from nationalized banks at a concessional interest rate of repo-rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for the present, with a tenure of 10 years.
  3. Included RESCO/Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA) Models.

The year-wise budgetary allocation and funds released under the PMSG: MBY is given below: -

As a result of various the measures taken to accelerate the deployment of RTS systems under the scheme, a total of 39,72,447 RTS system has been installed covering 48,02,717 households as on 22.7.2026.

While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 households reported even zero electricity bills for some months, depending on their self-consumption of electricity.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi

Government has been promoting convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with suitable Central and State programmes and funding sources, wherever feasible, to facilitate wider adoption of the schemes. For instance, PM KUSUM scheme guidelines allow for convergence with other central schemes including:

  • Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme for access of easy financing
  • Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) for solarization of segregated agriculture feeders
  • Promotion of micro irrigation techniques and Per Drop More Crop scheme
  • Replacement of agriculture pumps with energy efficient pumps
  • Gram Urja Swaraj Campaign to enhance self-sufficiency at village level

Similarly for PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, the convergence is taken up with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), for implementing the Solar Didi Programme under which women Self-Help Group (SHG) members under DAY-NULM are trained. Convergence of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) funds is also encouraged with PM Surya Ghar for eligible beneficiaries, particularly BPL households, PMAY beneficiaries and other vulnerable sections.

The Ministry has already issued communications and possible areas of convergence to all the states for convergence of PM KUSUM and PMSG Schemes with scheme of Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development etc.

This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi

The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) is a demand-driven scheme wherein all residential consumers in the country including the rural households, having a grid-connected electricity connection with the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits of the scheme, for installation of rooftop solar (RTS) systems by applying on the National Portal (www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in) of the scheme.

During the year 2025-26, a total of 18. 71 lakh RTS systems have been installed with a cumulative installed solar capacity of 6.7 GW, benefitting 22.71 lakh households across the country, including the rural households under the PMSG: MBY.

Under the PMSG: MBY, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 39,72,447 RTS systems have been installed, benefitting 48,02,717 households across the country including the households in rural areas, as on 22.07.2026.

While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 lakh beneficiaries have been reported by DISCOMs across the country, including the rural households to receive zero electricity bill after installation of RTS systems under the scheme during the any month/billing period, depending on their self-consumption of electricity.

Apart from installation of rooftop solar plants in residential sector, the PMSG: MBY also envisage installation of RTS plants in Government and commercial buildings including educational and health institutions, however, no central financial assistance (CFA) is provided to these categories of consumers as installation of rooftop solar plants is financially viable for them even without CFA.

This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

Patel “Hepatitis B birth-dose coverage…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry observes World Hepatitis Day 2026; marks eight years of National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP)
Union MoS for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel calls for a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat; urges collective action by Government, States and stakeholders to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030
India among the few countries providing free-of-cost treatment for Hepatitis C and management of Hepatitis B; access and affordability of services strengthened: Smt. Patel
“Hepatitis B birth-dose coverage crosses 92%; States should ensure 100% Hepatitis B screening of pregnant women and strengthen awareness on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C”
Over 21 crore beneficiaries screened, over 6 lakh patients treated, 1,153 treatment centres established and 7.64 crore pregnant women screened under NVHCP: Union Health Secretary
NVHCP leverages convergence with the Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Programme and the National AIDS Control Programme
IEC materials on viral hepatitis, modes of transmission and services available under NVHCP released at the event
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare today observed World Hepatitis Day 2026 under the global theme “Hepatitis: Let’s Break It Down”, marking eight years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). Launched on World Hepatitis Day in 2018 under the National Health Mission, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the programme reflects India’s commitment to eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, in line with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 3.3. Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare & Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, delivered the keynote address, and reaffirmed the Government of India’s commitment to a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat, and called for intensified efforts by the Government, States and all stakeholders to achieve the goal.

Delivering the keynote address, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated that “India is marking eight years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme, during which substantial progress has been made in prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.” She noted that “India is among the few countries providing free-of-cost treatment for Hepatitis C and management of Hepatitis B, while continuing to improve access and affordability of services.” She further highlighted that “the cost of medicines has been reduced to less than one dollar, while quality diagnostics are being made increasingly accessible to facilitate early identification and timely treatment.”

The Minister said that the programme has been expanded in a phased manner. Initially, treatment services for uncomplicated cases were strengthened at district health facilities, while selected institutions were strengthened to provide referral services for complicated cases. Thereafter, screening and treatment services were expanded to the country's network of more than 1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, thereby expanding access to hepatitis services at the primary healthcare level.

Highlighting preventive interventions, Smt. Patel noted that “the Hepatitis B vaccine, introduced under the Universal Immunization Programme in 2011, has achieved more than 92 percent birth-dose coverage.” She emphasised that “while around 65 percent of pregnant women are currently being screened for Hepatitis B, States and Union Territories should work towards 100 percent screening to ensure timely administration of the Hepatitis B birth dose for all eligible newborns and Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (HBIG) within 24 hours for newborns of Hepatitis B-positive mothers.”

The Minister also stressed the importance of vaccinating healthcare workers to prevent occupational transmission and called for focused interventions among high-risk populations to protect vulnerable groups from chronic liver disease and liver cancer. Describing Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C as “silent killers”, she underlined the need to generate greater public awareness and urged States and Union Territories to educate communities that testing and treatment services are available at government health facilities.

Reaffirming that “health is a shared goal”, Smt. Patel said that “the Government of India, State Governments and all stakeholders must continue working together with renewed commitment to achieve the goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030.” Expressing confidence in the country’s collective efforts, she stated that “sustained and intensified efforts would help realise the vision of a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat.”

On the occasion, Smt. Patel also released Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials, including posters on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, highlighting modes of transmission and services available under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP) for dissemination across States and Union Territories.

Addressing the gathering, Union Health Secretary, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, highlighted the significant progress achieved under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme. She informed that more than 21 crore beneficiaries have been screened, while over 6 lakh patients have received free treatment under the programme.

The Union Health Secretary highlighted that “the programme has surpassed its target of establishing one treatment centre in every district. With the support of States and Union Territories, the country now has 1,153 treatment centres, including more than 70 specialised treatment sites providing advanced care.” She also emphasized that “these achievements have been possible through a whole-of-government, whole-of-ministry and whole-of-society approach.”

Emphasizing the programme’s convergence-based implementation, Smt. Srivastava underlined that the National AIDS Control Programme supports outreach to high-risk populations, while the Universal Immunization Programme provides the Hepatitis B birth dose as well as vaccination of healthcare workers. She further highlighted that maternal health programmes prevent mother-to-child transmission through antenatal screening of pregnant women and administration of HBIG to newborns of Hepatitis B-positive mothers.

She informed that as a result of these coordinated efforts, more than 7.64 crore pregnant women have been screened, while 2.24 lakh newborns born to Hepatitis B-positive mothers have received HBIG. Stressing the need for intensified efforts, she called for identification and linkage to care of every infected individual and emphasised effective utilisation of the NVHCP Case-Based Management Information System (CPMIS), integrated with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), to strengthen patient tracking, treatment and follow-up, thereby helping prevent further transmission of the disease.

Speaking on the occasion, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, NHM, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, highlighted that the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme focuses on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, with interventions aimed at preventing mother-to-child transmission of Hepatitis B through antenatal screening and HBIG administration to newborns of infected mothers, and ensuring early detection and treatment of Hepatitis C, particularly among high-risk groups, including Injecting Drug Users (IDUs). She further noted that the programme is being implemented through convergence with the Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Programme and the National AIDS Control Programme, while expanding its convergence towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). She also added that the IEC materials released during the event would strengthen awareness and outreach efforts across States and Union Territories.

The Director General of Health Services (DGHS), Dr. Lavneet Gopal Krishna; Joint Secretary, National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP), Shri Nikhil Gajraj; WHO Representative to India, Dr. Yvan J.-F. Hutin; Deputy Commissioner, NVHCP, Dr. Sandhya Kabra; Additional Chief Secretaries (Health) and senior officers of the Ministry were also present on the occasion. The event was also attended virtually by Principal Secretaries (Health), Mission Directors from States and Union Territories, programme officers, experts and other stakeholders.

 

****

SR

HFW/Union Health Ministry Observes World Hepatitis Day 2026/28July2026/1

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Operation of PMBJP
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

The objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) are as follows:-

  1. To make available quality medicines and medical devices and consumables at affordable prices for all and to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure of consumers/patients.
  2. To popularise generic medicines among the masses and dispel the prevalent notion that low priced generic medicines are of inferior quality or are less effective.
  3. To ensure easy availability of the menstrual health services to all women across India.
  4. Generate employment by engaging individual entrepreneurs in the opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras.

Health and socio-economic impact assessment on the contribution after the operation of this scheme has not been conducted. However, the Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the implementing agency of the PMBJP scheme, undertakes continuous evaluation of Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) on the basis of their sale performance. Such evaluation, along with the performance of the scheme, indicates that PMBJP has significantly improved access to quality generic medicines at affordable prices as well as generating entrepreneurship opportunities across the country, through a rapidly expanding network of 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras.  

In the last 12 years, estimated savings of about ₹45,000 crore have accrued to citizens, when compared against the prices of branded medicines, contributing significantly to a sharp reduction in out-of-pocket expenditure by households and improving access to affordable medicines across the country. 

As on 30.06.2026, a total of 202 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened in the State of Assam. The district-wise number of JAKs opened the State of Assam is at Annexure.

In the last 12 years, the number of Kendras have increased from 80 in 2014 to 20,149 till 30.06.2026. Further, the sales have increased from 7.29 Crore in 2014 to 2252.19 Crore in F.Y.2025-26. On an average, 15 lakh people visit Jan Aushadhi Kendras daily.

Further, in order to promote acceptability and to increase sale of medicines supplied through JAKs, targeted awareness campaigns about the benefits of Janaushadhi medicines are conducted on a regular basis:

  1. Awareness campaigns: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), conducts awareness campaigns in coordination with bodies and platforms such as the Central Bureau of Communication, PIB, MyGov and MY Bharat, in various modes such as print, television, radio, social media platforms, outdoor hoardings, community engagement, etc.
  2. Interactive messages/calls: Outreach and citizen engagement are also pursued through WhatsApp chatbot and outbound calls to inform citizens regarding the quality of Janaushadhi products and the large savings that accrue from purchase of the same from nearest JAK.
  3. Jan Aushadhi Week: Jan Aushadhi Week is celebrated every year in the first week of March during which special campaigns such as public rallies, health camps, seminars in pharmacy colleges, children engagement programmes, etc. are conducted across the nation to educate citizens, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders about the benefits of Janaushadhi generic medicines.
  4. Messages from eminent persons: Audio/video messages from well-known persons such as public representatives and eminent doctors are disseminated on social media platforms to highlight the benefits of Janaushadhi medicines and dispel myths associated with respect to their quality.
  5. Public engagement programme in rural areas: To educate citizens in local languages/dialects, publicity is also done through health camps, nukkad-natak, audiovisual display at Common Service Centres and public engagement workshops in association with local JAKs in rural areas.

The Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the implementing agency of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, is accountable for monitoring the operation and functioning of Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country.  Monitoring of JAKs is carried out through a centralized IT-enabled system, regular review of sales and stock position, field inspections by PMBI officials and its representatives, and periodic interactions with Kendras.

There is no separate district-level monitoring agency under the district administration exclusively designated for monitoring the operation and functioning of Jan Aushadhi Kendras. 

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi

As on 30.06.2026, a total of 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across the country. The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojna has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, covering all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals. The medicines under PMBJP are made available at rates that are about 50% to 80% cheaper than those of branded medicines.

During the financial year 2025-26, sales of medicines with MRP worth ₹2,252.19 crore have been made under the Scheme.  In the FY2026-27, sales of MRP value ₹474.40 crore have been made till 30.06.2026

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Strengthening pharmaceutical and bulk drug manufacturing in Maharashtra
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has implemented following schemes to strengthen pharmaceutical and bulk drug manufacturing throughout the country, including in the State of Maharashtra:

  1. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals: This scheme aims to enhance India’s manufacturing capabilities by increasing investment and production in the sector and contributing to product diversification to high-value goods in the pharmaceutical sector. Under the scheme, 55 companies/pharmaceutical entities have been selected for production of approved products under eligible product categories. Further, 60 manufacturing units pertaining to 14 approved applicants are located in the State of Maharashtra. As of March 2026, the scheme has attracted cumulative investment of ₹45,774 crore. The scheme has contributed to generation of employment to the tune of 1,16,884 persons till March, 2026.
  1. PLI Scheme for promotion of domestic manufacturing of critical Key Starting Materials (KSMs) / Drug Intermediates (DIs) / Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) in India (also known as the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs): This scheme aims to avoid disruption in supply of critical active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs which are used to make critical drugs) for which there are no alternatives and there is excessive dependence on a single source. Under the scheme, 48 projects have been approved, out of which 3 projects are in the State of Maharashtra. As of March 2026, the scheme has attracted an investment of ₹5,070.45 crore.  The scheme has contributed to generation of employment to the tune of 5,226 persons till March,2026.
     
  2. Under Scheme for Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks, three parks have been approved in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, through their respective State Implementing Agencies. The total project cost of these is over ₹6,300 crore, with Central assistance to the tune of ₹1,000 crore each for creation of common infrastructure facilities. The stated objectives of the Scheme include creation of common infrastructure facilities, achieving economies of scale, boosting competitiveness of the domestic bulk drug industry, and reducing import dependence.
     
  3. The Scheme for "Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma MedTech sector (PRIP)" has been launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, with the goal of transforming India into a global powerhouse for R&D in the Pharma MedTech sector. The scheme has a total financial outlay of ₹5000 crores, which includes ₹700 crores to establish Centers of Excellence (CoEs) at seven National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education & Research (NIPERs), and ₹4200 crores to accelerate investments in the R&D ecosystem within the sector.

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Price regulation of essential medicines
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi

Prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order 2013 (DPCO, 2013). As per extant provisions of DPCO, 2013, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) fixes the ceiling prices of the drugs included in the Schedule-I of DPCO, 2013 which is based on the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) published by Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW). NLEM, 2022 contains 388 medicines, listed under 29 therapeutic categories. NPPA has fixed ceiling prices for 935 scheduled formulations as on 23.07.2026. NPPA also fixes retail prices of new drugs as defined in para 2(1)(u) of DPCO, 2013, i.e., formulations launched by existing manufacturers of a medicine listed in NLEM by combining it with another drug, or by changing the strength or dosage or both of such medicine. The retail prices of new drugs are applicable to the applicant manufacturer and marketer and they cannot sell the new drug above the price notified by NPPA. Retail prices of 3,845 new drugs have been fixed by the NPPA till 23.07.2026. Further, in case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers are required to not increase their maximum retail price (MRP) of a formulation by more than ten percent of the MRP of that formulation during the preceding 12 months. In addition, NPPA can also fix the prices of any drug under Para 19 of DPCO 2013 in public interest in extra-ordinary circumstances. Details of prices fixed or revised by NPPA are available on NPPA’s website (www.nppa.gov.in).

NPPA continuously reviews the affordability and availability of medicines. As and when required, Government invokes the provisions of DPCO, 2013 and makes required interventions to ensure affordability and availability of essential medicines.

To prevent overpricing, DPCO 2013 requires every manufacturer of a formulation to print the maximum retail price on the label of the container of such formulation. Further, no person is permitted to sell any formulation to any consumer at a price exceeding the price specified on the current price list or price indicated on the label of the container or the pack thereof, whichever is less. Moreover, NPPA monitors the prices of both scheduled and non-scheduled formulations on an ongoing basis and takes action in accordance with the provisions of DPCO, 2013 against companies that are found overcharging consumers, based on references received regarding overcharging from any source, including Price Monitoring and Resource Units set up in States, State Drugs Controllers, samples purchased from open market, reports from market database and complaints lodged through various grievance redress channels.

Government has taken various measures to improve the access of essential medicines at affordable rates to the common man which include the following:

  1. The Government has launched the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana scheme under which quality generic medicines is provided through more than 20,000 Janaushadhi Kendras at rates that are typically 50% to 80% cheaper than branded medicines.
  2. Under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, health assurance/insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year is provided for secondary or tertiary care hospitalisation, including for medicines.
  1. Under the Free Drugs Service Initiative of the National Health Mission, essential medicines list recommended under the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) are made available free of any charge at public health facilities ranging from Primary Health Centres (PHCs) to district hospitals across the country.
  2. Under the Amrit (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment)

initiative of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, affordable medicines are provided for the treatment of cancer, cardiovascular and other diseases, implants, surgical disposables and other consumables etc., at an average discount of up to 50% on market rates through AMRIT Pharmacy stores set up in number of hospitals and healthcare institutions.           

  1. Financial assistance is provided to poor patients belonging to families living below the poverty line, who suffer from major life-threatening diseases including cancer, under the umbrella scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi and the Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant.

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

Further, as a follow-up, Department of Financial Services (DFS) conducts periodic and regular meetings with RRBs and sponsor banks at various levels.

The agenda items for the review meetings, inter-alia, include:

  1. Review of the performance of RRBs on financial parameters.
  2. Focus on technology upgradation.
  3. Thrust on Micro Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME) portfolio.
  4. Importance on loan diversification towards Agri-allied, MSME and Retail Sectors.
  5. Expansion of Financial inclusion in rural and remote areas. 

The financial health of RRBs has improved in the recent years. RRBs posted the highest ever consolidated net profit of Rs. 10,177 crores during FY 2025-26. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Rising prices of life saving drugs
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi

Presently, prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order 2013 (DPCO, 2013) based on the National Pharmaceuticals Pricing Policy, 2012. As per extant provisions of DPCO, 2013, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) fix the ceiling prices of the drugs included in the Schedule-I of DPCO, 2013 which is based on the National List of Essential Medicines and the retail price of new drugs as defined in para 2(1)(u) of DPCO, 2013. Further, in the case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers are required to not increase the maximum retail price (MRP) of such formulation by more than 10% of the MRP of that formulation during preceding 12 months. In addition, NPPA also fixes the prices of drugs under Para 19 of the DPCO, 2013 in case of extra-ordinary circumstances and in public interest. Instances of overcharging are dealt with as per the provisions of DPCO, 2013. Details of prices fixed or revised by NPPA are available on NPPA’s website (www.nppa.gov.in).

NPPA monitors availability of drugs in the country and takes remedial measures whenever an issue of non-availability of any medicine is brought to its notice through various sources including State Drugs Controllers (SDCs), Pharma Jan Samadhan Portal, NPPA helpline and public grievance portals and individuals. In addition, Government has taken other measures to improve the access of essential medicines at affordable rates to the common man which include the following:

  1. The Government has launched the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana scheme under which quality generic medicines is provided through more than 20,000 Janaushadhi Kendras at rates that are typically 50% to 80% cheaper than branded medicines.
  1. Under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, health assurance/insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year is provided for secondary or tertiary care hospitalisation, including for medicines.
  1. Under the Free Drugs Service Initiative of the National Health Mission, essential medicines list recommended under the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) are made available free of any charge at public health facilities ranging from Primary Health Centres (PHCs) to district hospitals across the country.
  1. Under the Amrit (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) initiative of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, affordable medicines are provided for the treatment of cancer, cardiovascular and other diseases, implants, surgical disposables and other consumables etc., at an average discount of up to 50% on market rates through AMRIT Pharmacy stores set up in number of hospitals and healthcare institutions.
  1. Financial assistance is provided to poor patients belonging to families living below the poverty line, who suffer from major life-threatening diseases including cancer, under the umbrella scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi and the Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant.

The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS 5.0) in May, 2026, to tide over any short-term liquidity mismatches faced by businesses due to West Asia Crisis. The scheme provides guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) for the amount in default under the additional credit facility extended to the eligible borrowers. The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage for MSMEs and 90% guarantee coverage for non-MSMEs and the scheduled passenger airline sector, up to a credit flow of ₹2,55,000 crore, which includes ₹5,000 crore specifically earmarked for the scheduled passenger airline sector.

Under ECLGS 5.0, borrowers in the airline sector are eligible for assistance of up to 100% of their total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26, i.e., from 1.1.2026 to 31.3.2026 (both dates inclusive). The maximum loan amount available under ECLGS 5.0 for the airline sector is ₹1,500 crore per borrower (of this, any amount beyond ₹1,000 crore and Up to ₹1,500 crore shall be permitted only with a proportionate equity contribution from the promoters/owners).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
FUNDS TO NFIES
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has approved the National Forensic Infrastructure Enhancement Scheme (NFIES) with a total financial outlay of ₹2254.43 crore from financial year 2024-25 to 2028-29. Under the scheme, ₹1309.13 crore have been allocated for setting up of 09 campuses of the National Forensic  Sciences  University  (NFSU) and ₹860.3 crore for setting up of 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs). Funds to the tune of ₹119.09 crore have been released and utilized under the scheme for the NFSU campuses and for CFSLs. The Scheme is being implemented centrally for creation and strengthening of forensic infrastructure at identified locations.

Under the scheme, setting up of 09 campuses of the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) has been approved in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal. Further, setting up of 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs) has also been approved in Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Kerala. 06 CFSLs at Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar are to be co-located with the NFSU campus. So far, land for NFSU campus / CFSL has been allotted in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh).

The NFSU campuses are currently operational from Transit buildings allotted in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Khordha (Odisha), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), and Jaipur (Rajasthan). There is no proposal for setting up of CFSL in Andhra Pradesh.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

Cell Broadcast Alert System for Disaster Warnings is operated through the Integrated Alert System based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) implemented by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The system   integrates   five   Warning   Generating   Agencies,  namely the India

Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE) and Forest Survey of India (FSI), with the State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) of all States/UTs. The respective Warning Generating Agencies and SDMAs are responsible for issuing and authorising disaster-specific alerts, while the CAP-based platform facilitates their dissemination through the Cell Broadcast system.

The Cell Broadcast Alert will be used for timely warning to citizens for disaster events with very short lead time like Cyclone, Tsunami, Heavy Rainfall, Lightning, Flash Flood, Thunderstorms, Hailstorm, Avalanche, Cloudburst, Industrial/man-made disasters and other events which merit immediate alerting. The Warning generating agencies provide Geo-targeted warnings and Geo-targeted alerts are disseminated to the public.

Timely receipt of warning and timely dissemination of alerts acts as one of the contributing factor in reducing disaster-related causalities and improving emergency preparedness. The System provides timely alerts to the public, which indirectly improves emergency preparedness and necessary precautions, thus helps in reducing disaster-related casualties.

All warnings generated by the forecasting agencies are translated to the State language of the target population and disseminated to the recipients by the SDMAs. The Alerts are received across all mobile networks and handsets in the geo-targeted area which includes remote and vulnerable areas.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
NATIONAL DRUG CONTROL VISION
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi

To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The four key focus areas outlined in the Vision Document are as under: -

  1. Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations)
  2.  Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control
  3.  Demand & Harm Reduction
  4.  Capacity Building & Coordination

Specific actionable points for the States/UTs including State of Assam and Andhra Pradesh along with the timelines have been   detailed in the Vision Document. It is further envisaged that States and Districts would prepare their vision for 3 years Road Map to control drugs in consonance with the National Road Map outlined in the Vision Document.

The Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) envisages a comprehensive framework for capacity building, awareness and preventive interventions. It focuses on strengthening the institutional capacity of States, Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTFs), forensic laboratories and NCB, enhancing inter-agency coordination through the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism. Further, under Demand and Harm Reduction, the Vision Document seeks to strengthen the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA)

through large-scale awareness and preventive initiatives in educational institutions and communities, including awareness campaigns, training of teachers, counsellors and healthcare professionals, promotion of drug-free campuses, consent based screening as part of student welfare programme, establishment of Anti-Drug Committees, appointment of anti-drug officers and institutional mechanisms for early identification, counselling and referral of students, through various Ministries in the Government.

The Vision Document envisages training of law enforcement officers, forensic experts, healthcare professionals, teachers, sensitization of students and judicial officers on drug abuse prevention.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
CFCFRMS 2.0 PLATFORM
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints.

To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint processing, bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026.

‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule  of  the    Constitution   of   India.    The  States/UTs   are  primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation, and prosecution of crimes including establishment of cyber forensic laboratories through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs). The Central Government supplements the initiatives of the States/UTs through advisories and financial assistance under various schemes for capacity building of their LEAs.

Cyber crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing of chargesheets, arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by the State/UT Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of the law.

A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores.

CERT-In issues alerts and advisories regarding latest cyber threats/vulnerabilities      including     malicious    attacks    using    Artificial Intelligence and countermeasures to protect computers, networks and data on an ongoing basis.

AI driven situational awareness systems are deployed by CERT-In to detect malicious domains and phishing activities for necessary mitigation.

CERT-In operates an automated cyber threat intelligence exchange platform for sharing tailored alerts with organisations across sectors for proactive threat mitigation.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has released financial assistance  to the tune of Rs. 132.93 crores under the ‘Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC)’ Scheme, to the States/UTs for their capacity building such as setting up of cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories, hiring of junior cyber consultants and training of LEAs’ personnel, public prosecutors and judicial officers. Cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories have been commissioned in 33 States/UTs including Maharashtra and more than 24,600 LEAs personnel, judicial officers and prosecutors have been provided training on cyber crime awareness, investigation, forensics etc.

The state of the art National-Digital Investigation Support Centre (previously   known   as  National  Cyber  Forensic Laboratory (Investigation) {NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of the I4C, at New Delhi (on 18.02.2019) and at Assam  (on 29.08.2025) to provide  early stage cyber  forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has provided its services to State/UT LEAs in more than 14,064 cases pertaining to cyber crimes.

At present, 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories and 28 State Forensic Science Laboratories including in Maharashtra are operational across the country to assist in investigation of cybercrime cases. Assistance has been provided to 20 States / UTs for Strengthening of Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA Analysis and Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs.

Till 30.06.2026, a total of 1,586 entities have been onboarded onto the CFCFRMS platform, including 40 foreign banks operating in India.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
KHADI PRODUCTS TO CAPF
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:19PM by PIB Delhi

In order to promote the procurement and daily use of  Swadeshi and Khadi products, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has been registered with Kendriya Police Kalyan Bhandar (KPKB) since 13th March 2020. Also a  number of steps have been taken in the direction:-

(i)  Four items, i.e (i) Mustard Oil (ii) Cotton Bed Durries (iii) Woolen Blanket and (iv) Bed Sheet and Pillow Cover have been identified for procurement by CAPFs from Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

(ii)      ITBP is the Nodal Force for procurement of Mustard Oil and Durries. CRPF is the Nodal Force for procurement of Blankets, and ADG (Medical), CAPFs, is the Nodal for the procurement of Bed Sheet and Pillow Cover.

(iii)     Swadeshi and Khadi products are also being sold through Master Bhandars and Subsidiary Bhandars of KPKB for the benefit of serving and retired personnel of CAPFs all over India.

(iv)     Daily use items are procured by the CAPFs from the KVIC.

(v)      The National Bee Board is continuously providing necessary support and training to all forces for scientific beekeeping. Gardens are being developed within the premises of the Central Armed Police Forces by planting more flowering plants to create a suitable environment for honey production. Honey produced through beekeeping is being used as food for the soldiers to enhance their health and immunity.

Under Vibrant Village Programme-II (VVP-II), CAPFs have started procuring edible items such as fruits, vegetables, dairy products, dry rations and meats from Self-Help Groups (SHGs) & State Cooperative Societies of border areas.

The comprehensive details of the Civic Action Programme (CAP) allocations and welfare activities conducted by the CAPFs in border areas are given at annexure-I. In addition to above, allocations and welfare activities conducted CAP particularly in Darjeeling and Kalimpong districts are given at annexure II & III respectively.

ANNEXURE - I

  1. Repairs to community buildings, viz, schools, hospitals, health centers, community hall etc.
  2. Constructions of tracks, small bridges, culverts, mines, cableway, water supply, electrification schemes, playground etc.
  3. Running of health, medical, dental, veterinary camps which include providing of medical equipment and stores etc. to existing hospitals nursing homes.
  4. Human Resources Development to include imparting of vocational training, conduct of educational excursions to students to places of national interest and to organize career counseling training and coaching etc.
  5. Initiation of small projects in improvement and care of livestock, beekeepeing, fisheries, agricultural techniques, orchards, forestry carpet and or handloom weaving, history etc.
  6. Sanitation and Hygiene through Extension Services and social education.
  7. Drinking water basic precaution and system of storage.
  8. Development of sources of non-conventional energy.
  9. Development of handicraft and cottage industries.
  10. Assistance during Natural Calamities.
  11. Water harvesting structure.
  12. Sports facilities.
  13. Distribution of Transistor.
  14. Pre-recruitment training.
  15. Implementation of ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan’ for which activities include programmes to sensitize the people through higher educational institutions, university campuses and schools by organizing cultural and sports events in coordination with NGOs and master volunteers working in field.
  16. Provisions of a standard set of community use items such as cooking utensils, basic furniture (chairs, tables), shamiyanas etc.
  17. Provision of computer and furniture to Schools.
  18. Cost of transportation of stores for execution of the above-mentioned tasks.
