Commonwealth Games

India has remained one of the strongest performers at the Commonwealth Games. The country won 64 medals at Glasgow 2014 and improved to 66 at Gold Coast 2018. India followed this with 61 medals at Birmingham 2022. Wrestling, weightlifting, table tennis, badminton and athletics have consistently contributed to India's success. PV Sindhu, Vinesh Phogat and Achinta Sheuli have been among the country's notable performers.

India's growing global success reflects the strength of its sporting ecosystem and the determination of its athletes to excel on the world stage.

 

Commonwealth Games 2026

The Commonwealth Games 2026 are being held in Glasgow from 23 July to 2 August 2026. The Games have brought together athletes from 74 countries across a 10-sport programme, including six fully integrated Para Sports, hosted at four venues.

India is represented by a 124-member contingent, comprising 78 male and 46 female athletes. The contingent reflects the country's growing depth of talent across multiple sporting disciplines.

As of 27 July 2026, India has won four medals, comprising one gold, two silver and one bronze. Jhandu Kumar opened India's medal account with a bronze in para powerlifting. Rishikanta Singh became the first able bodied Indian medallist after winning silver in the men's 60 kg weightlifting event. He also set a new Commonwealth Games record in the snatch.

Mirabai Chanu delivered another historic moment by winning India's first gold medal in Glasgow. The victory marked her third consecutive Commonwealth Games title. Muthupandi Raja also added to India's medal tally with a silver in the men's 65 kg weightlifting event.

With several events still to be contested, Indian athletes continue to compete with determination and confidence. The nation looks forward to more memorable performances as the Tricolour flies high in Glasgow.

The Pursuit of Sporting Excellence

India's sporting journey continues to gather momentum. Sustained investment, stronger support systems and focused athlete development are creating a lasting foundation for success. Rising participation and improved performances at international competitions reflect the impact of these efforts. With the Commonwealth Games 2026 still underway, Indian athletes continue to compete with determination and pride. Every performance inspires the next generation to dream bigger and aim higher. As India looks to the future, the nation remains committed to building champions and strengthening its place among the world's leading sporting nations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Public Consultations on Budget, NEP, Data Protection and Aadhaar Reforms Bring Citizens Closer to Policy Making
Over 6.32 Crore Citizens Participate in Governance Through MyGov
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

MyGov platform was launched by the Government of India as a citizen engagement platform. It collaborates with multiple Government bodies/ Ministries to engage people in policy formulation and seeks the opinion of people on issues/ topics of public interest and welfare.

For citizen engagement, the platform facilitates multiple features such as discussions, creative tasks, polls, surveys, and on-ground activities.

The MyGov platform has seen significant growth in its user base and engagement metrics. It has continued to actively host Consultations (Discussions), Polls, Surveys across key national initiatives, ensuring sustained citizen participation in governance as depicted below:

3,57,431

MyGov serves as a facilitative platform for citizen participation. Discussions and other engagement activities on the platform are owned and proposed by various Ministries and Departments. Once these consultations are concluded, the compiled opinions and suggestions are shared with the concerned ministry/department for their consideration during formulating or reviewing policies, schemes, or programmes.

 

A few of the recent public consultations hosted on the platform include National Education Policy (NEP)-2020, Digital Personal Data Protection Bill-2022 and Draft Digital Personal Data Protection Rules-2025, Union Budget Consultations, Draft Amendments to the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules-2020, Reforms in the Examination Process (National Testing Agency), Draft Data Centre Policy-2020 and Draft New Textiles Policy-2020, Memorandum for the 8th Central Pay Commission.

 

The final examination, acceptance, and incorporation of citizen suggestions into Government policies, programmes, or administrative actions remain the prerogative of the respective Ministries and Departments.

 

To assess the effectiveness of its citizen engagement initiatives, third-party Impact Assessment studies have been carried out in 2017 and 2025. These studies concluded that MyGov has significantly expanded the scope of public participation through its diverse engagement models. Based on the recommendations of these assessments to improve inclusivity and accessibility, MyGov has implemented several strategic enhancements:

 

● Multilingual Support: The platform has been made available in 12 languages (English and 11 Indian regional languages) to bridge linguistic barriers

● Mobile Accessibility: A dedicated MyGov mobile application was launched to cater to the large number of mobile users in the country

● Enhanced Outreach: Digital and social media presence has been strengthened to ensure governance remains transparent and result-oriented

● Platform Usability: The web interface is periodically updated to enhance user experience and general accessibility

 

MyGov compiles the feedback /suggestions/recommendations of citizens and forward these to the concerned ministries/departments for their necessary action. Decisions regarding Action Taken Reports and any consequential policy or programme changes fall within the jurisdiction of the respective ministries/departments that own the specific policy/programme/scheme.

 

MyGov periodically reviews feedback specifically related to the functioning of its platform. This ensures that features, multilingual support, and general accessibility are continuously improved to meet the evolving needs of citizens and maintain a robust bridge between the Government and the public.

 

This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, Shri Jitin Prasada in Rajya Sabha on 24.07.2026.

****

Dr. Nayan Solanki / Kanishk Sharma / Vanshita Jaiswal

It is aimed at creating economic…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions
13 Responsible AI Projects, 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 27 India Data & AI Labs Strengthen Safe & Trusted AI under IndiaAI Mission
India's Safe & Trusted AI Pillar Powers Responsible Innovation while Shaping Global AI Governance
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

IndiaAI Mission: India’s AI policy is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of democratizing technology. It is aimed at creating economic opportunities and employment for youth, while addressing risks associated with AI.

 

Accordingly, the Government approved the IndiaAI Mission in March 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371 crore over five years to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in the country.

 

The Mission comprises seven pillars viz. IndiaAI Compute, Foundation Models, AIKosh, IndiaAI

Application Development Initiative, FutureSkills, Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI.

 

Progress under IndiaAI mission till date:

 

AI models: Government of India is supporting Indian startups and institutions to develop large language models. 20 indigenous sovereign model proposals have been identified for support, comprising 12 LLMs and 8 SLMs. Notable successes so far include:

  • Sarvam AI’s Sarvam 30 billion parameter and 105 billion parameter models
  • Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model
  • BharatGen’s multilingual foundation models
  • Avataar AI’s video generation model

 

Domain-specific SLMs, including specialized models and AI frameworks addressing healthcare, language technologies and agentic AI systems are at various stages of development and deployment.

 

Affordable compute:

  • Compute service providers empanelled: 15
  • Number of projects supported: 237
  • GPU hours sanctioned: 93 lakh GPU hours
     

Application Development:

  • 12 National-level Hackathons/Innovation Challenges launched.
  • Supported the development of 62 AI prototypes and 20 AI solutions deployment
     

Talent development:

  • 686 fellowships have been awarded across undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes in 178 institutions.
  • YUVA AI for All programme has been completed by over 26 lakh individuals.
     

IndiaAI labs:

  • 27 India Data and AI Labs have been established, which has supported training for more than 2500 students
  • Work ongoing on additional 188 labs.

 

AI Centres of Excellence:

58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) being established across States and Union Territories in collaboration with the respective State/UT Governments and industry partners.

 

Safe & Trusted AI pillar

At the same time, the Government is also cognizant of the risks associated with AI. The Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission aims to promote the responsible development, deployment and adoption of AI through indigenous governance frameworks, standards, tools and evaluation mechanisms.

 

13 Responsible AI projects have been approved in educational institutions across the country. These include topics such as bias mitigation, machine unlearning, privacy-preserving AI, explainability, deepfake detection and AI risk assessment.

 

Key initiatives include:

  • Saakshya, multi-agent framework developed by IIT Jodhpur &  IIT Madras for deep fake detection
  • AI Vishleshak for improving Audio-Visual forgery detection system
  • IIT Kharagpur’s project on Real-Time Voice Deepfake Detection System

 

Nature & Objectives of projects related to bias mitigation, explainability, privacy preserving Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning:

  • Bias Mitigation: NIT Raipur is developing responsible AI algorithms to reduce bias in medical image analysis, clinical decision-making and healthcare applications
  • Privacy-Preserving & Explainable AI: IIT Delhi (with IIIT Delhi and IIT Dharwad) is developing privacy-preserving machine learning models using federated learning.
    • Defence Institute of Advanced Technology (DIAT) is is building explainable & privacy-preserving AI for security applications
  • Machine Unlearning: IIT Jodhpur is developing techniques to remove remove unwanted, sensitive or outdated information/concepts from generative foundation models

 

Overall, these projects are aimed at making AI fairer, more transparent, privacy-preserving, secure and trustworthy.

•  The AI Safety Institute has been established for AI safety, security and developing trust with diverse stakeholders, engaging academia, startups, industry and Government bodies through a hub-and-spoke model.

• The India AI Governance Guidelines lay down a risk-based governance framework addressing algorithmic bias, misinformation, deepfakes and unintended societal harm, and propose institutional mechanisms including the AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG), Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) and AI Safety Institute (AISI) for oversight, standards and safety research.

 

The IndiaAI Safety Institute was announced in January 2025 to advance science-based and indigenous research on AI safety and governance. The Institute is responsible for promoting the safe, secure, inclusive and trustworthy development, deployment and adoption of AI in India.

 

It also oversees the implementation of projects selected under the two rounds of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar.

 

India's approach to responsible AI is anchored in the vision of "AI for All". It seeks to harness AI for inclusive development while ensuring that it remains safe, trusted, and aligned with India's socio-economic priorities.

  • India actively engages with global processes on AI governance, including Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), G20, and United Nations, to ensure that international norms reflect the perspectives and priorities of the Global South
  • As Chair of the India AI Impact Summit 2026, held in New Delhi, India contributed in shaping the global agenda on responsible AI through key deliverables:
    • As part of New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments, leading AI developers made voluntary commitments on the safe and responsible development of frontier AI
    • Guidance Note on AI Governance, oﬀered practical guidance to countries on designing context-appropriate AI governance frameworks
    • Trusted AI Commons, a shared repository of open resources to democratise access to safe and trusted AI

 

These outcomes reflect India's commitment to shaping global norms on AI governance while protecting its strategic and developmental interests.

 

This information was submitted by Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Rajya Sabha on 24.07.2026.

 ****

Dr. Nayan Solanki / Kanishk Sharma / Vanshita Jaiswal

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC
Over 1.38 lakh new employers and more than 1.12 lakh new employees added under SPREE Scheme between July 2025 and January 2026
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has launched the Scheme to Promote Registration of Employers/Employees (SPREE 2025) from July 2025 to January 2026.  Under the Scheme, a one-time opportunity was provided to employers and employees of organised sectors who may have been inadvertently left out from ESI coverage to register without concern for retrospective coverage or punitive action. A total of 1,38,718 new employers and 1,12,72,772 employees have been added during the Scheme till 31.01.2026.

ESIC has undertaken several initiatives across the country to strengthen healthcare infrastructure, improve access to quality medical services and enhance social security benefits for ESI beneficiaries. These include enhancement of bed strength, procurement of advanced medical equipment, establishment of ICU/HDU facilities, operationalisation of new hospitals and dispensaries, empanelment of private and super-specialty hospitals, upgradation of digital platforms for OPD appointments, Aadhaar-based authentication for delivery of benefits, online submission of cash benefit claims, collaboration with Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) for providing secondary and tertiary healthcare services where ESIC facilities are not adequately available.

ESIC has also recently operationalised/upgraded hospitals at Ompora (Jammu & Kashmir), Doddaballapur (Karnataka), Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu), Surat (Gujarat), and expanded hospitals at Sanath Nagar (Telangana), Beltola (Assam) and Rajamahendravaram (Andhra Pradesh).

This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of Labour & Employment
 SPECIAL DRIVE FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS DISPOSAL OF LONG-PENDING LABOUR CASES
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) has launched a three-month Special Drive from 1st June, 2026 to 31st August, 2026 for the expeditious disposal of pending industrial dispute cases and claim cases relating to wages, gratuity, maternity benefits and other statutory claims.

As on 1st June, 2026 a total of 16,033 cases were pending before the field offices. During the first month of the Special Drive, 2,769 cases have been disposed of.

This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
ATAL BEEMIT VYAKTI KALYAN YOJANA
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has approved extension of the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) from 01.07.2026 to 30.06.2027.

The eligibility criteria to avail benefit under the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) is as under:

  1. The insured person must be in insurable employment for a minimum period of 12 months immediately before his/her unemployment and should have contributed for not less than 78 days in one completed contribution period in 12 months immediately preceding to unemployment.
  2. The unemployment must not arise from misconduct, during lock out, superannuation, or convicted for false statement under the provision of ESI Act, 1948.

Several steps to expedite the settlement of claim under the scheme have been taken. These include online submission and processing of the claims, direct benefit transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of beneficiaries and regular monitoring of claim settlement to ensure timely disbursal of benefits.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Kosi–Mechi Intra-State Link Project has been included under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayi Yojana – Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (PMKSY-AIBP) for balance cost of works of Rs. 6,143.22 crore, with central assistance of Rs. 3,652.56 crore. The project is scheduled for completion by March 2029.  The remodeling work of Eastern Kosi Main Canal from K.M. 0.00 to 41.30 has been taken up at an awarded contract value Rs. 2639.80 crore.  Physical progress of 8.5% has been achieved so far.

The Government of India is engaged in regular dialogue with the Government of Nepal regarding construction of dams on the Kosi River for the mutual benefit of both countries, including flood control. A Joint Project Office (JPO-SKSKI) was constituted in 2003 with the mandate to prepare the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Sapta-Kosi Multipurpose Project and Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project. The status of preparation the DPRs of these projects is as under.

  1. Sapta Kosi Multipurpose Project: The work of topographical surveys, construction material survey, water quality survey, inland navigation studies, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,258m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed.

  2. Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project: The work of topographical surveys, water quality survey, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,549m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed for Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project.

Further, no meeting of Indo-Nepal Joint Committee was held during 2025-26.

Central assistance of Rs. 206.77 Crore has been released to the State of Bihar under the Flood Management and Border Areas Programme during last three years.

No proposal for a permanent Kosi-Gandak basin authority is under consideration of the Government of India.

The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

***

ND

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
   “MUSEUM GRANT SCHEME AND PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE”
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Culture operates Museum Grant Scheme under which financial assistance is provided for setting up of New Museums/development of the existing museums/digitization of museum collections/setting up of virtual museums and training of museums professionals of museums managed by Central/State Governments, Societies, Autonomous bodies, Public sector Undertaking, local bodies, Academic Institutions and Trusts registered under the societies Act at the regional, State and District Level in the country.

Eligibility Criteria: For the purpose of support under this component, museums have been classified into three categories as per the existing guidelines of the Museum Grant Scheme:

 

  1. Category I: Central or State Government owned museums in State Capitals including Museums owned by Public Sector Undertakings.
  2. Category II: Central or State Govt. owned museums including Museums of Public Sector Undertakings
  3. Category III: All other museums including Museums of Public Sector Undertakings

Category I: Existing renowned Museums of the Central or State Governments located in the state capitals, subject to the following:

  1. The museum must be located in the capital of the state/union territory.
  2. It must be of high repute, having a significant collection of objects/artefacts.
  3. It must have had an annual footfall of 1 lakh visitors per annum in the preceding 2 years.

Category II: Central or State Govt. owned museums including museums of PSU

Category III: Projects of Societies, Autonomous bodies, local bodies, Public Sector Undertaking, Academic Institutions and Trusts registered as a society under the Indian Societies Act of 1860 (XXI) or a similar legislation of the state governments, or as a Public Trust under any law at the time being in force subject to the following:

  1. It should have been in existence for at least three years prior to the application. However, this condition can be relaxed in exceptional cases at the discretion of the Expert Committee, the reasons for which should be recorded in writing;
  2. It should have a well-defined constitution and laid down rules/bye laws for its   functioning
  3.  It should be in ownership and possession of a substantial collection of objects of historical and / or cultural importance for display in the museum.
  4. It should be able to maintain the Museum and bear all recurring costs;
  5. It should have the necessary infrastructural facilities, resources and     personnel to execute the work for which the grant is required;
  6. It should produce a certificate from the State Government (Department of   Culture or equivalent) attesting to its satisfactory performance;
  7. It should not be run for personal profit.
  8. It should be the owner of the land on which the museum is situated or proposed to be constructed, which should be easily accessible to visitors. 

 

Ministry of Culture, Government of India may take up   any project under Category I &II as project of National importance at its discretion for the purpose of development of Museum & Cultural Spaces.

The details of proposals received during the last five years are at Annexure-I. The proposal approved, and grants released under the Museum Grant Scheme for setting up of new museum and development of existing museums during the last five years are at Annexure- II.

 

Under the Museum Grant Scheme financial assistance is being provided to:

 

  1. Museums having collection of Antiquities, Numismatics, Paintings, Ethnological collections, Fold Art and others including Art & Crafts, Textiles, Stamps etc.
  2. Online Virtual Museums displaying objects in any or all the disciplines and
  3. Theme based Museums
  4. Virtual Experiential Museums
  5. Projects of National Importance.

 

Ministry of Culture provides financial assistance to the project proposals received for digitalisation of museum collections as per guidelines of the Museum Grant Scheme.

 

Further, The Ministry of Tourism promotes India as a holistic destination in the tourism generating markets to promote various Indian tourism products and tourism destinations of the country, including Museums, to increase India’s share of the global tourism market. The promotion is carried out through organizing and participating in travel events and exhibitions; providing assistance to State Governments for organizing fairs and festivals; inviting influencers, tour operators, journalists and opinion makers to visit the country under the Hospitality Programme of the Ministry; various outreach activities through website and social media; promotions in association with the State Governments and the overseas Indian Missions etc.

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

As informed by the Government of Gujarat, the proposed Gulf of Khambhat (Kalpasar) Project is an ambitious water resources initiatives of the State Government. The project envisages the creation of one of the world's largest coastal freshwater reservoirs through the construction of a dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. Upon implementation, the project is expected to significantly augment the availability of freshwater and substantially mitigate water scarcity in the Saurashtra region by providing a dependable source of water for irrigation and other identified uses.

The project includes a proposed highway-cum-rail corridor over the dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. As per the present project layout, the corridor is expected to reduce the travel distance between Bhavnagar and Surat by approximately 179 km, from about 356 km through the existing land route to about 177 km via the proposed dyke corridor, thereby improving regional connectivity and reducing travel time.

As informed by the State Government of Gujarat, Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Kalpasar Project is at an advanced stage of finalization. The ongoing Indo-Dutch technical cooperation is expected to further strengthen the DPR by incorporating international best practices and advanced technical expertise in areas such as coastal engineering, hydraulic modelling, salinity management, climate resilience and water management. This collaboration is intended to enhance the technical robustness of the project and facilitate informed decision-making during its implementation.

The project envisages development of approximately 2,470 MW of hybrid renewable energy capacity on reclaimed land that is presently submerged during high tide. The renewable energy generated is proposed to be utilized, inter alia, for pumping freshwater to meet irrigation requirements in the coastal regions of Saurashtra. DPR incorporates appropriate engineering measures, hydraulic studies and salinity management strategies to address the issue of salinity ingress.

The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

***

ND

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
“MUSEUMS AND MEMORIALS ON INDIAN FREEDOM MOVEMENT”
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi

The details of the Museums, Memorials and interpretation centres dedicated to the Indian freedom movement, freedom fighters and the national independence struggle is given at Annexure.

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) undertakes maintenance and upgradation of museums and exhibitions relating to India's freedom movement, subject to requirement. ASI organises outreach programmes on important occasions such as Independence Day, Republic Day, World Heritage Day and Week and International Museum Day, in association with local schools, educational institutions and heritage stakeholders, to create awareness among children and youth about the legacy of India's freedom movement. 

Further, various programmes/exhibitions are carried out throughout the year as per the events in the museums of the Ministry of Culture to preserve and promote the legacy of India's freedom movement.

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Gyan Bharatam Mission and Manuscript Digitisation
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, National Manuscript Survey was launched across all States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. However, any district-wise target was not set for the survey and physical registration of manuscripts under the Mission. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported.

 Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses AI (Artificial Intelligence) enabled technologies, including Large Language Script Models (LLSM), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR), script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation, to provide intelligent access to India’s manuscript heritage.

Gyan Mitram, the AI-powered knowledge interface of the Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses LLSM, OCR, HTR, script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation to enable intelligent interpretation, contextualization and exploration of manuscripts by integrating manuscript images, transcriptions and translations.

BharatiyaGPT, features “Manuscript-to-Conversational AI” on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal converting manuscript heritage into AI-ready, machine-readable knowledge and provides a multilingual and multimodal access, including text, audio and voice-based interaction through its “Talk to Manuscript” feature, thereby making India’s knowledge traditions more accessible to scholars, students, researchers and the public.

 

Pandulipi Darpan is an AI driven tool on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal that enables users to upload or select a digitized manuscript image and access AI-assisted script recognition, transliteration and translation.


Access to digitized copies of manuscript is facilitated in accordance with applicable laws and the rights of custodians and rights holders. Wherever legally permissible, manuscripts and associated metadata may be made available for public and scholarly research through the National Digital Repository, while sensitive, restricted or rights-protected materials may be subject to appropriate access conditions.

 

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

***

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Manuscript Clusters and Partner Institutions under Gyan Bharatam   Initiative
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Gyan Bharatam Mission (GBM) has been mandated to establish a nation-wide network of Cluster Centers (CCs) and Independent Centers (ICs) across the country. These institutions have been selected based on prescribed criteria, including the size and significance of manuscript collections, institutional capacity, availability of qualified manpower and infrastructure, regional representation, and experience in manuscript-related activities. A list of CCs/ICs onboarded so far is at annexure.

National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported. The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is over 8 lakhs, out of which, more than 3.90 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access in view mode.

 

  The year-wise budget sanctioned and allocated under GBM is as hereunder:

Gyan Bharatam, is a Pan-India initiative covering cataloguing, conservation, digitization and publication of manuscripts identified across the country. For effective implementation, a framework of Cluster Centres and Independent Centres has been envisaged. These centres are provided financial assistance in form of grant-in-aid to undertake manuscript related activities as elaborated above. The list of onboarded centers in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana is at annexure.

Gyan Bharatam envisages the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, research, publication and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage irrespective of script, language, dialect, tradition, community or geographical location. Eligible repositories having manuscripts are considered for onboarding with GBM in accordance with the Mission guidelines, subject to physical verification, institutional readiness and availability of resources, funds etc.

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

item.category: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
item.description: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates CWG 2026 bronze medal-winner powerlifter Jhandu Kumar The para powerlifter received INR 10 Lakh cash award from Hon’ble Union Sports Minister; Jhandu said he was overjoyed when Hon’ble Prime Minister congratulated him on social media for his performance Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi Hon’ble Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitated para powerlifter Jhandu Kumar, who won India’s first medal in the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, at his residence…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates CWG 2026 bronze medal-winner powerlifter Jhandu Kumar
The para powerlifter received INR 10 Lakh cash award from Hon’ble Union Sports Minister; Jhandu said he was overjoyed when Hon’ble Prime Minister congratulated him on social media for his performance
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitated para powerlifter Jhandu Kumar, who won India’s first medal in the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, at his residence on Monday. Jhandu won bronze in the men’s heavyweight category with a best lift of 190kg.

Dr Mandaviya handed INR 10 Lakh as cash award to Jhandu, who comes from a humble background in Nalanda district in Bihar. Talking about his experience of meeting the Union Sports Minister, the powerlifter said: “I felt privileged to meet the Union Sports Minister today. How many people get to meet a central minister in their lifetime. I never wondered that I will be felicitated for my achievement in sports. Dr Mandaviya asked me about my experience in Scotland. It was a great feeling to interact with him.”


 

Jhandu sold vegetables and even rode an e-rickshaw to support his family in Harnaut town of Nalanda before being selected by chief para coach Rajender Rahelu to train at SAI NCOE Gandhinagar back in June 2023. 

He said that when Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted about his achievement on social media, it gave him goosebumps. “I have not had much sleep since the time I have won a medal, due to the excitement and adrenaline rush. My phone has been buzzing throughout. I was overwhelmed when our Hon’ble PM wrote about me on social media. I think Indian sports has reached this level all thanks to his continuous encouragement and support for athletes. I think I was the only CWG medallist who received encouragement from his country’s Prime Minister,” the 29-year-old said.

Prior to his Glasgow glory, the powerlifter won back-to-back silver and gold medals in the Khelo India Para Games 2024 and 2025 editions respectively. The Khelo India athlete has now trained his eyes on the upcoming Asian Para Games scheduled from October 18 to 24, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. 

“When you receive such support and backing from the country’s leadership, you get motivated to perform even better. I will go to my hometown for a brief period to meet my family members before returning to Gandhinagar in order to prepare for Asian Para Games. China are a strong contender but I will do my best to secure a medal for my country, I promise,” Jhandu signed off.

*****

Ayushman Kumar

(Release ID: 2289907)

item.title: NHAI Successfully Defends Major Arbitration Case to Safeguard Public Funds in National Highway Projects
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
item.description: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Successfully Defends Major Arbitration Case to Safeguard Public Funds in National Highway Projects Against claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores raised by the concessionaire, the Arbitral Tribunal awarded only Rs. 46 crores plus applicable interest to settle the case Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi Achieving a significant legal and financial milestone, NHAI has secured a favorable outcome in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a concessionaire promoted by M/s Era Infra…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Successfully Defends Major Arbitration Case to Safeguard Public Funds in National Highway Projects
Against claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores raised by the concessionaire, the Arbitral Tribunal awarded only Rs. 46 crores plus applicable interest to settle the case
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

Achieving a significant legal and financial milestone, NHAI has secured a favorable outcome in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a concessionaire promoted by M/s Era Infra Engineering Limited for 151 km long Bareilly – Sitapur BOT (Toll) project in Uttar Pradesh which was terminated by NHAI in May 2019. The Arbitral Tribunal substantially upheld the position of NHAI, thereby safeguarding public resources and reaffirming the contractual framework governing National Highway projects.

The three-member Arbitral Tribunal examined claims and counterclaims arising out of the concession agreement for the project. The Concessionaire had raised 30 claims aggregating to around Rs. 3,177 crores. After detailed consideration, the Tribunal allowed only three claims amounting to Rs. 46 crore plus applicable interest, while rejecting majority of the claims.

Arbitration Tribunal upheld the Supplementary Agreement (SA) dated 30th March 2015 and decided that project delays were concurrent and majority of the Concessionaire's claims were rejected.  NHAI also filed counterclaims, including claims relating to financial losses and public inconvenience. While these counterclaims were not allowed by the Tribunal, NHAI successfully defended itself against the overwhelming financial claims raised by the Concessionaire, resulting in a substantial protection of public funds.

In a series of recent notable legal wins, NHAI has successfully defended various arbitration cases. In June 2026, arbitration case related to Tumkur–Chitradurga 6 laning Project in Karnataka, was awarded in favour of NHAI for Rs. 1,202 crores. Also in April 2026, two arbitration cases in Panipat–Jalandhar Highway Project involving Concessionaire’s claims of around Rs. 8,375 Crores and counterclaims of NHAI for Rs. 2,888.64 Crores were settled for Rs. 819.96 Crores in favour of NHAI.  Similarly in May 2026, arbitration case related to 6 laning of Kamrej–Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat in which claims of around Rs. 174.49 crore raised by the contractor, was settled for only Rs. 54 lakhs by the Arbitral Tribunal.

The successful outcome of arbitration cases underscores NHAI's focus on robust contractual management and effective legal strategy. It also reinforces NHAI’s resolve to ensure effective utilisation of public funds while maintaining transparency and contractual discipline in the development and management of National Highway infrastructure.

***

GDH/DS

(Release ID: 2289902)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Digital Skill Development Platform
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has developed Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for the skilling ecosystem under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). Launched on 13th September 2023, it brings the entire skilling ecosystem onto a single unified platform, integrating training, assessment, certification, employment and entrepreneurship services, while allowing training providers, employers and government schemes to onboard onto a common interoperable ecosystem. Built on a mobile-first approach and interoperable with other Government platforms such as National Career Service, eShram, DigiLocker and BHASHINI, SIDH advances the Government's vision of a unified, citizen-centric skilling ecosystem accessible to all.

 

As per Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) data, a total of 35,17,023 learners are registered under PMKVY 4.0, 52,98,397 under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), 10,19,992under the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme, and 4,96,755 under the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative. A total of 78,647 trainers holding a valid Trainer ID are registered on the platform. Further, 13,633 training centres are registered under PMKVY 4.0 (Short Term Training and Special Projects), 296 training centres under the JSS scheme, and 13,888 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) are onboarded on SIDH. The key courses available on the platform span short-term skilling and apprenticeship programmes under PMKVY 4.0 and NAPS, community-based training under JSS, and foundational and applied Artificial Intelligence courses under SOAR. The number of youth registered, trained/oriented, certified and employed through the platform, State/UT wise, including in Punjab, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, particularly Nabarangpur and Bastar Lok Sabha Constituencies, is given at Annexure-A.

 

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), has launched the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative to equip learners, educators and the workforce with foundational Artificial Intelligence (AI) knowledge and practical competencies. The initiative comprises nationally recognised, NSQF-aligned, fully online and self-paced AI courses delivered through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) by NCVET-recognised Awarding Bodies. Subsequently, SOAR has been expanded beyond foundational AI literacy to include AI and AI application-oriented courses focused on AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualised AI applications for the informal sector. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 4,96,426 learners have enrolled and 98,576 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH).

 

The Government has undertaken several measures to ensure effective access to digital skilling platforms, including the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), for citizens across rural, remote and aspirational districts. SIDH serves as a one-stop digital platform for accessing skilling, certification, apprenticeship and employment-related opportunities through a single interface.

 

To facilitate wider outreach and accessibility, the Government has adopted an integrated online and offline approach, including multilingual awareness campaigns, digital outreach, community mobilisation through Panchayats and Common Service Centres, workshops, skill awareness activities and on-ground support initiatives. District Skill Committees are also involved in identifying local skilling requirements and facilitating training opportunities in rural and underserved areas. Further, initiatives such as Skill Hubs under PMKVY 4.0 and the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme provide skill training opportunities closer to the beneficiaries, including in aspirational, backward and remote regions.

 

To strengthen AI-based skill development and digital training infrastructure, the Government is promoting skilling in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Cloud Computing, Internet of Things, Data Analytics, Cyber Security and Green Technologies. Digital and blended learning models, industry partnerships and continuous upskilling and reskilling initiatives are being promoted to ensure access to industry-relevant and future-ready skills across the country.

 

Further, the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative has been designed as a fully online, self-paced AI learning programme to promote AI-enabled learning across the country through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH). The courses are NSQF-aligned and credit-linked under the National Credit Framework (NCrF), with credits being integrated with the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) to facilitate transparent recognition and accumulation of learning outcomes. This enables learners to access nationally recognised AI courses from anywhere in the country while promoting portability, transparency and lifelong learning within the skilling ecosystem.
